gm.title: Description
lines: A former watch captain who uses stolen martial techniques to run down weakened enemies for the Black Iron Pact.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Str +3, Dex +7, Wis +7. Skills Acrobatics +7, Athletics +3, Perception +7, Stealth +7. Passive Perception 17. Common.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Black Iron Pact actions, p. 364. Stat block, p. 365.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Evasion. For a Dexterity save that would halve damage, Qar takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Exploit Opening (3/day). Gain advantage on an attack roll Qar makes.
Supernatural Resistance. Qar has advantage on saves against powers, spells, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Unarmed Strikes. If the same creature is hit by all three, it is Dazed until the end of its next turn.
Unarmed Strike. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Iron Ring (2/day). Teleport to the Cyst. From inside the Cyst, teleport to somewhere Qar has visited.

gm.title: Reactions
lines:
No Survivors. When a visible enemy within 40 ft. drops to 0 HP, move up to Qar's speed. If he ends that move within 5 ft. of an enemy, he can make an Unarmed Strike against that enemy.
Voice Stealer (3/day). When an enemy within 30 ft. that Qar can hear finishes casting a spell with a verbal component, it must pass a DC 15 Intelligence save or lose the ability to speak for 1 minute, with an end-of-turn save.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Black Iron Pact. The party may use one villain party action per round after an enemy's turn. Each action is available once per encounter, in any order, and requires its performer to be present and able to act.
Action 1. Party Tactics. Qar and each ally within 60 ft. who can see or hear him can move up to their speed.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn a Dazed creature can move, take an action, or take a bonus action. It chooses one. Becoming Dazed during its turn ends the turn. Extra actions from effects such as Haste or Action Surge are still available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can remove Dazed.

gm.title: Description
lines: An Emerald Enclave guide based at Fort Beluarian who travels with the vegepygmy Kupalué. He deliberately takes routes through undead territory to help drive the undead out of Chult.

gm.title: Armor
lines: AC 11, or 16 while protected by Barkskin.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Druidic and two other languages. Qawasha and Kupalué use a private sign language with each other.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
4th-level druid, Wisdom, save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks. Treat him as a druid for magic item use and attunement requirements.
Cantrips (at will). Druidcraft, Produce Flame, Shillelagh.
1st level (4 slots). Entangle, Longstrider, Speak with Animals, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots). Animal Messenger, Barkskin.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage, or 4 (1d8) with both hands. While Shillelagh is active, the attack is +4 to hit and deals 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Guide
lines: Qawasha knows the jungle's plants and animals and can find campsites near Chwingas. When he guides an expedition, he deliberately seeks out undead-infested areas to clear them. He recommends buying an exploration charter before leaving Fort Beluarian because the Flaming Fist mistreats unlicensed explorers.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 35, handout 7 on p. 246. Use the Druid from Monster Manual (2014), p. 346, with the published errata.

gm.title: Statistics
lines: Speed · 40 ft., fly 80 ft., swim 40 ft.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Silent Decay uses acid and living shadows and wants to blot out the sun.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saving throws Con +14, Wis +10, Cha +11. Arcana +9, History +9, Perception +10, Stealth +8. Immune to acid and necrotic damage and to Charmed, Dazed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, and Stunned. Blindsight 120 ft., truesight 60 ft., passive Perception 20. Speaks Common and Draconic.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Breathes air and water.
Consume Shadow (3/day). Turn a failed save into a success. Dispel any magical darkness in the lair. Qazyldrath cannot use Enshroud or Thwart Healing until the end of their next turn.
Shadow Strength. Qazyldrath's acid and necrotic damage ignore resistance.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, 15-ft. reach, one target. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. Extinguish the target if it is a light source, or extinguish any light source the target holds or wears.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, 10-ft. reach, one target. Hit 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage. Qazyldrath can move the target up to 15 ft. horizontally.
Vacuous Breath (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 90-ft.-long, 20-ft.-wide line make DC 22 Dexterity saves, taking 24 (7d6) acid plus 24 (7d6) necrotic damage or half on a success. The area fills with magical darkness for 1 minute. Darkvision cannot see through it. Daylight or a light-producing spell of 5th level or higher can illuminate it.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Enshroud. A creature Qazyldrath sees within 120 ft. makes a DC 19 Dexterity save. On a failure, it is Blinded and vulnerable to necrotic damage until the start of their next turn.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Thwart Healing. When a creature within 60 ft. regains HP, it regains half as much on a failed DC 19 Constitution save.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Each action is available once per encounter, after an enemy finishes a turn. Use them in any order, at most one per round.
1. Burning Globs. Enemies they see within 90 ft. make DC 19 Dexterity saves. Each creature that fails takes 14 (4d6) acid damage at the start of each turn until a creature uses an action to remove the globule from itself or another creature it can reach.
2. Shadow Form. Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing until the end of their next turn, then teleport up to 120 ft. into an unoccupied space they see.
3. Sinking Gloom. Create a 5-ft.-deep, 20-ft.-radius pool of acid on visible ground within 120 ft. It is difficult terrain and lasts 1 minute. An enemy starting a turn inside takes 24 (7d6) acid damage and must pass a DC 19 Strength save or become Restrained until the start of its next turn. An enemy starting its turn flying within 30 ft. of the pool makes a DC 19 Dexterity save. On a failure, it lands in the nearest open space of its choice in the pool, takes 24 (7d6) acid damage, and is Restrained until the start of its next turn.

lines: Uses the verified Flee, Mortals! stat block for this creature. Check this publication for encounter-specific changes.
Coronal Hollow has three separate lair actions: Acidic Gas, Consume Light, and Hungry Gloom. These can change the lighting and interact with Qazyldrath’s shadow mechanics.

gm.title: Description
lines: An orichalcum wheel with blades that races through the Ancients’ ruins to drive off intruders.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 16. Stealth 13. Resistant to acid, fire, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Immune to poison and psychic damage, exhaustion, Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, and Poisoned. Keensense 120 ft. Understands the languages of the Ancients and Machine Speech and has no speech.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: STR +7 · DEX +3 · CON +4 · INT -3 · WIS +6 · CHA -3

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Construct Nature. The guardian needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Construct Resilience. The guardian ignores poison and psychic damage, exhaustion, and the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, and Poisoned conditions.
Wheelie Maneuverable. Moving out of an enemy’s reach provokes no opportunity attacks. The guardian can fit through spaces large enough for a Small or Medium creature without squeezing.
Overdrive (46 HP or fewer). Once it hits this threshold, the guardian gains advantage on melee weapon attacks and its attackers gain advantage against it. This lasts until it has more than 51 HP.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make four Whirling Blade attacks or two Flame Jet attacks.
Whirling Blade. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 10 (1d12 + 4) slashing damage.
Flame Jet. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit 21 (4d8 + 3) fire damage.
Acid Spray (Recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make a DC 15 Dexterity save against 31 (7d8) acid damage, taking half on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Stunning Jolt. When a visible creature within 5 ft. hits the guardian with a melee attack, force it to make a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure the attacker is Stunned through the end of its next turn. Each time it takes damage while Stunned this way, it can repeat the save and end the effect on a success.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Shapechanger. The quasit can use its action to polymorph into a beast form that resembles a bat (speed 10 ft. fly 40 ft.), a centipede (40 ft., climb 40 ft.), or a toad (40 ft., swim 40 ft.), or back into its true form. Its statistics are the same in each form, except for the speed changes noted. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Magic Resistance. The quasit has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Claws (Bite in Beast Form). Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take 5 (2d4) poison damage and become poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Scare (1/Day). One creature of the quasit’s choice within 20 feet of it must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the quasit is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success. Invisibility. The quasit magically turns invisible until it attacks or uses Scare, or until its concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell). Any equipment the quasit wears or carries is invisible with it.

gm.title: Bloodmoon (Ex)
lines: On the three nights of the full moon, set Dex to 16 and Ref to +5. Use the bracketed printed AC 15, touch 13, flat-footed 12. Witnesses to the change may require a DC 15 Ravenloft Horror save. Unfamiliar melee weapons such as polearms and warhammers do not benefit from Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Horror save
lines: Use Will against DC 15 with applicable modifiers. Failure by 1–5 gives a minor Horror effect, 6–10 a moderate one, and 11 or more a major one. Roll 1d4 on the corresponding Horror table. Failure by 16 or more also calls for an immediate DC 10 Madness save. See Ravenloft Player’s Handbook, pp. 77–83.

gm.title: Description
lines: An oak with a face in its bark can spy through the surrounding grove. It drags prey toward its trunk with roots that reach far beyond its branches.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any forest. Solitary or pair. Usually neutral. Standard treasure. Speaks Sylvan and may know other languages. Advancement 9–16 HD (Huge), 17–21 HD (Gargantuan).

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative −2. AC components −2 size, −2 Dex, and +13 natural. Touch 6, flat-footed 21. Base attack +6, grapple +17. Space 10 ft., reach 5 ft. or up to 90 ft. with roots. Fort +11, Ref +0, Will +4.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Plant traits, DR 10/bludgeoning or slashing, electricity resistance 20, and fire resistance 20. Camouflage (Ex). Spot, Survival, or Knowledge (plants or herbs) DC 16 to identify it before it attacks. The stat line lists blindsight 120 ft. The dedicated trait gives 60 ft. for sensing corporeal objects and creatures, in addition to normal sight.
A distressed quickwood can drum loudly enough to be heard a mile or farther.

gm.title: Skills
lines: Hide −8, Intimidate +10, Listen +12, Sense Motive +11, Spot +12, Survival +12. Add +18 racial to Hide in a forest.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +17 melee (1d6 + 11). Full attack. Eight slams +17, each for 1d6 + 11. It can attack with one root per HD. Roots extend 30 ft. each round, to a maximum of 90 ft. Each root is Medium, AC 15, with 8 HP tracked separately. It withdraws every root when half are severed.
Improved Grab and Constrict (Ex). A root slam hit allows a grapple. A successful grapple check deals 1d6 + 11 constriction damage to a Medium or smaller foe. Pull grappled foes 30 ft. per round toward the trunk. It can bite an adjacent grappled target once each round at +10 melee (1d4 + 5).
Animate Trees (Sp, at will). Control up to four normal oaks within 180 ft. Each spends a full round uprooting itself, then moves at speed 10 ft. and fights as a 3.5 treant. A tree stops moving if the quickwood is incapacitated or leaves range. As a standard action it can scry through oaks out to 1 mile. Otherwise use liveoak at caster level 12th.
Channel Fear (Su). As a free action when directly targeted by a spell, the quickwood can force all creatures within 45 ft. to make a DC 15 Ravenloft Fear save or become panicked. The spell is lost if its caster fails this save. It resolves normally if the caster succeeds or is outside the radius.

gm.title: Table notes

gm.title: Description
lines: The ghost of a cleric or paladin keeps vigil over the spot where its quest failed. Its light can blind a traveler before they see the figure inside.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC +2 Dex, +3 deflection. Touch AC 15, flat-footed AC 13. Printed base attack +6, grapple +6. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +13.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +6 melee (1d6). Full attack. Two slams +6 melee (1d6 each).
Blinding Pulse (Su). Once per minute, use a gaze attack. A failed DC 18 Fortitude save deals 1d10 damage and permanently blinds as the blindness spell at caster level 10. The victim’s corneas bear skull-shaped scars that add 1 to Outcast Rating when visible.
Frightful Moan (Su). As a standard action, force living creatures within 30 ft. to make a DC 18 Fear save. Evil creatures take a −5 morale penalty. A success grants immunity to this spirit’s moan for one day.
Sunbeam (Su). Three times per day, use sunbeam at caster level 10.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Incorporeal and undead traits, +4 turn resistance.
Radiant Aura (Su). The spirit sheds light as bright as daylight. Its continuous 30-ft. gaze blinds for 1d4 rounds on a failed DC 18 Fortitude save. It cannot suppress the aura.
Rejuvenation (Su). If destroyed, it reforms in 2d4 days. Completing its unfinished quest lays it to rest permanently.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Diplomacy +18, Knowledge (religion) +20, Listen +17, Search +20, Sense Motive +18, Spot +17. Alertness, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Toughness.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land or underground, within 1 mile of the site of its death. Solitary, always lawful evil, no treasure. Advances to 11–20 HD (Medium). Speaks languages it knew in life. It may let sympathetic travelers pass and refuses to speak to evil creatures.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Blinding Pulse gives no separate range. Use the standard 30-ft. gaze range.
The text both says it immediately attacks disrespectful intruders and describes its intended victims as evil. Its continuous gaze cannot be suppressed.

gm.title: Description
lines: Radlee deserted after her commander used her unit as bait. As a Soulbinder, she protects her fellow mercenaries and has little patience for Ellan’s courtly demands.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Plate. Saving throws Str +10, Con +5, Wis +6. Athletics +10, Intimidation +4, Perception +6, Survival +6. Truesight 60 ft., passive Perception 16. Speaks Common.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Exploit Opening (3/day). Gain advantage on an attack roll.
Sure-Footed. Advantage on saves against forced movement or being knocked Prone.
Tactical Vigilance. Radlee has advantage on initiative checks. While she can act, she and allies within 30 ft. who see or hear her cannot be surprised.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Halberd attacks, three Longbow attacks, or one Halberd attack and use Backswipe.
Halberd. Melee weapon attack +10, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 12 (1d10 + 7) slashing damage.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack +6, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.
Backswipe. One creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 18 Strength save. On a failure it takes 16 (3d10) bludgeoning damage and falls Prone.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Protector. When a creature Radlee can see within 10 ft. attacks her ally, she can make a Halberd attack against the attacker.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Soulbinders. The party can use one villain party action per round, after an enemy's turn. Each action is available once per encounter, in any order. The member taking it must be present and able to act.
Action 2, Strategic Positioning. Radlee and each ally within 60 ft. who sees or hears her can move up to half speed without provoking opportunity attacks and take the Hide action.

gm.title: Recoverable Magic Item
lines:
Visionary’s Cloak. Very rare. Attunement required. The wearer has advantage on initiative checks and cannot be surprised. With the hood up, the wearer has truesight to 60 ft. and glowing eyes. Raising or lowering the hood takes an action.
Cursed Sentience. The item uses its Soulbinder's alignment, mental ability scores, and languages. It hears and sees in darkness within 60 ft. and can speak to its wearer telepathically. Break attunement with Remove Curse or equivalent magic. After seven days attuned and every 24 hours after that, make a DC 18 Wisdom save. Each failure reduces Wisdom by 1 while attuned. On the third failure, the Soulbinder takes control and changes the wearer's body, statistics, and equipment to match its own. The wearer remains aware. Breaking attunement restores the body and control. The Soulbinder returns to the item when attunement ends or the body dies. After 1d6 + 12 months of possession, the victim's soul and body are destroyed. The full group ritual for permanently lifting the curse is on p. 382.

gm.title: Description
lines: The winged demon who leads the Cult of Rakdos carries a flaming scythe and prizes a performance he has never seen before.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Necrotic. Rakdos also resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Captivating Presence. Any creature starting its turn within 30 ft. of Rakdos makes a DC 25 Wisdom save. On a failure, it becomes charmed by Rakdos for 1 minute or until it gets farther than 30 ft. from him. A successful save grants immunity to Captivating Presence for 24 hours.
Cruel Entertainment. When a creature Rakdos can see within 60 ft. drops to 0 HP, he gains 25 temporary HP.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Rakdos can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Magic Resistance. Rakdos has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Rakdos’s weapon attacks are magical.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
Rakdos casts with Charisma (save DC 25) and needs no material components.
At will. Hellish Rebuke (cast at 5th level).

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks with Curtain-Call Scythe or Claw.
Curtain-Call Scythe. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 24 (3d10 + 8) slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) fire damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d8 + 8) slashing damage.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Rakdos has three legendary actions and regains them at the start of his turn. He can use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Sadistic Revelry (1 action). Each ally of Rakdos or creature charmed by him within 60 ft. must use its reaction. It moves up to half its speed toward the nearest creature it can see if it is more than 5 ft. away, then makes one melee attack against that creature if able.
Scythe (2 actions). Use Curtain-Call Scythe.
Touch of Pain (3 actions). Make one Claw attack against a creature within 10 ft. The target makes a DC 25 Constitution save. On a failure it is poisoned for 1 minute and cannot maintain concentration while poisoned this way. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Lair context
lines: Rakdos sometimes withdraws for months or years to his lair below the guildhall. The book describes the retreat on p. 246.

lines: Limited Magic Immunity. The rakshasa can’t be affected or detected by spells of 6th level or lower unless it wishes to be. gm.title: Traits
lines: Greater Magic Resistance. The rakshasa automatically succeeds on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and the attack rolls of spells automatically miss it. Without the rakshasa’s permission, no spell can observe the rakshasa remotely or detect its thoughts, creature type, or alignment. Fiendish Restoration. If the rakshasa dies outside the Nine Hells, its body turns to ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Fane of the Night Serpent
lines: Ras Nsi can enter any of the five disks in areas 8–12 and continue moving from any other disk in the temple. In his quarters (area 12), he can use a bonus action to say “Ssilum” and animate five shields. They initially raise his AC by 10. When they turn a hit into a miss, one drops and the bonus falls by 2. Only Ras Nsi can activate them, and their effect stays in his quarters. Once all five drop, he needs a long rest before using them again. Sekelok is his bodyguard. Acererak promised to help him free Dendar in exchange for protecting the tomb. If the party can show that stopping the death curse would help him, Ras Nsi may let them proceed.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Description
lines: A commander among Tiamat's devils, a red abishai leads troops in the Nine Hells or takes control of a cult that has strayed from her orders.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Devil's Sight. The abishai sees through magical darkness out to the range of its darkvision.
Magic Resistance. The abishai has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Claw attack. The abishai can also use either Frightful Presence or Incite Fanaticism.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 38 (7d10) fire damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d10 + 6) force damage plus 11 (2d10) fire damage.
Frightful Presence. The abishai chooses creatures within 120 ft. that are aware of it. Each makes a DC 18 Wisdom save. On a failure it is frightened of the abishai for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds or recovers gains immunity to this abishai's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Incite Fanaticism. Choose up to four other creatures within 60 ft. that can see the abishai. Until the start of its next turn, each has advantage on attack rolls and is immune to the frightened condition.
Power of the Dragon Queen. Choose one Dragon the abishai can see within 120 ft. The Dragon makes a DC 18 Charisma save with disadvantage if it is chromatic. A success grants immunity to this ability from this abishai for 1 hour. On a failure the Dragon is charmed by the abishai for 1 hour and treats it as a trusted friend to heed and protect. Damage from the abishai or one of its companions ends the charm.

Claw. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage.

Frightful Presence. Each chosen creature within 120 ft. that is aware of the abishai must make a DC 18 Wisdom save or be frightened of it for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. On a success or when the effect ends, the creature is immune to this abishai’s Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
Incite Fanaticism. Choose up to four allies within 60 ft. that can see the abishai. For 1 minute, those allies have advantage on attack rolls and cannot be frightened.
Power of the Dragon Queen. Choose a dragon the abishai can see within 120 ft. The dragon makes a DC 18 Charisma save. Chromatic dragons save with disadvantage. A success grants immunity to this abishai’s Power of the Dragon Queen for 1 hour. On a failure, the dragon is charmed for 1 hour and treats the abishai as a trusted friend to heed and protect. The charm ends if the abishai or its companions damage the dragon.

lines:

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:

Attack (1 action). Make one Claw or Tail attack.
Wing Attack (2 actions). Each creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its flying speed.
Arcane Spear (3 actions). Create four spears of magical force. Each spear hits a creature the greatwyrm chooses and can see within 120 ft., dealing 12 (1d8 + 8) force damage before disappearing.

gm.title: Mythic actions
lines:

Bite (1 action). Make one Bite attack.
Chromatic Flare (2 actions). Each creature in a 60-ft.-radius sphere centered on the greatwyrm must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity save or take 22 (5d8) fire damage.

gm.title: Description
lines: Red slaadi gather in Limbo to wrestle and reshape islands of drifting matter. When one meets a stranger, its mood can turn from play to hunger in moments.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Magic Resistance. The creature makes saving throws with Advantage against spells and other magical effects.
Regeneration. The slaad regains 10 HP at the start of each of its turns while it has at least 1 HP.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Injecting Claw attacks.
Injecting Claw. Melee attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage. A Humanoid hit by the claw makes a DC 14 Constitution save if it carries no slaad curse. On a failure it becomes cursed without realizing it, and the claw leaves an egg inside it. Ending the curse destroys the egg.
The egg develops over 2d4 × 10 days. During the last 24 hours the target feels ill, its Speed is halved, and it makes D20 Tests with Disadvantage. When that time ends, a Slaad Tadpole hatches and chews its way out, killing the host.

gm.title: Slaad control gems
lines:
A slaad born from the Spawning Stone carries a magical control gem in its head. Once another creature claims the gem, the slaad is Charmed and obeys the bearer. It stops being Charmed if the bearer or the bearer's allies harm it, if someone returns the gem to the slaad, or if Greater Restoration destroys the gem when cast on the slaad.
Wish can retrieve the gem. If the slaad fails its save against Imprisonment, the caster gets the gem and the slaad stays free. Removing the gem from an Incapacitated slaad takes 1 minute and a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Medicine) check. Failure deals 22 (4d10) Piercing damage to the slaad.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Monster Manual (2024), p. 285. The Slaad Control Gems sidebar supplies the control gem rules.

gm.title: Description
lines: A red slaad can leave an egg in a humanoid it claws. A growing tadpole uses that creature as its host.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Magic Resistance. The slaad has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn, the slaad regains 10 HP if it has at least 1 HP.
Control Gem. The slaad has a magical gem in its brain. It must obey the creature that possesses the gem and is immune to being Charmed for as long as the gem controls it. Destroying the gem ends this means of control.
Spell extraction. If the slaad fails a save against Imprisonment, the caster can have the spell move the gem to their open hand instead of imprisoning the slaad. Wish can retrieve the gem if cast in the slaad's presence with that wording. Greater Restoration cast on the slaad destroys the gem without injuring it.
Surgical extraction. A creature proficient in Wisdom (Medicine) can remove the gem while the slaad is Incapacitated. Each attempt takes 1 minute of uninterrupted work and a DC 20 Wisdom (Medicine) check. A failure deals 22 (4d10) psychic damage to the slaad.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (2d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. A humanoid hit by the claw makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure it contracts a disease by receiving a slaad egg.
Slaad Egg. A humanoid can carry only one egg to term at a time. The egg migrates to its chest and becomes a tadpole over three months. For the last 24 hours, halve the host’s speed and give it disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks and saves. The tadpole emerges over one round and kills the host. Curing the disease before emergence destroys the unborn tadpole.

gm.title: Slaad Control Gem
lines: A slaad created by a Spawning Stone has a control gem. A slaad that was born another way develops one on contact with the stone. Whoever holds the extracted gem can command the slaad, which is immune to being Charmed while under that control.

Wish can recover a gem, Imprisonment can transfer it on a failed save, and Greater Restoration destroys it harmlessly. A trained healer can spend 1 minute attempting extraction from an Incapacitated slaad with a DC 20 Wisdom (Medicine) check. On failure the slaad takes 4d10 psychic damage.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The Spawning Stone implants a color-matched gem in each slaad it creates. A slaad born elsewhere gains a gem only if it touches the Stone.

The listed skill totals include racial bonuses to Bluff, Diplomacy, and Sense Motive and, in spider form, to Jump and Spot. The widow also gains a +8 competence bonus to Hide and Move Silently around its webs. Alertness, Improved Initiative (bonus), Skill Focus (Bluff).

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Darkvision 60 ft.
Alternate Form (Su). As a standard action, assume its one specific humanoid form as if using polymorph. Gear stays as it is. Death restores spider form. A widow can switch forms while maintaining a pin.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Use the attack listed for the current form.
Poison (Ex). On a bite hit, Fortitude DC 15. Initial damage 1d6 Strength, secondary damage 2d6 Strength.
Fluid Drain (Ex). In spider form, pin a living creature using a successful grapple check to drain 1d4 Constitution per round the pin holds. Each Constitution point consumed sustains the widow for a day.
Web (Ex). Use the 3.5 Medium monstrous spider rules. Throw a web up to eight times per day as a net-like ranged touch attack (10-ft. range increment, 50-ft. maximum) against a target up to Large. A trapped creature can spend a standard action to attempt DC 12 Escape Artist or DC 16 Strength. A Medium web has 6 HP. A widow that wins an opposed Strength check against a webbed victim can pull it 10 ft. closer as a standard action.
Infest (Ex). A widow can implant 2d4 eggs in a paralyzed mate once a year and wrap the target in webbing. Remove the eggs before they hatch in 1d6 days. After hatching each young deals 1 HP of damage to the host per day. Immature young use monstrous spider statistics until they mature at one year.

lines: A Large aberration with challenge rating 10. Named abilities include Reduced Threat, Amphibious, Mucous Cloud.

lines: Saving Throws Con +4, Int +6, Wis +4 Skills History +10, Perception +8 Senses darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 20 Languages Deep Speech, telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The aboleth can breathe air and water. Mucous Cloud. While underwater, the aboleth is surrounded by transformative mucus. A creature that touches the aboleth or that hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature is diseased for 1d4 hours. The diseased creature can breathe only underwater. Probing Telepathy. If a creature communicates telepathically with the aboleth, the aboleth learns the creature’s greatest desires if the aboleth can see the creature.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The aboleth makes three tentacle attacks. Tentacle. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or become diseased. The disease has no effect for 1 minute and can be removed by any magic that cures disease. After 1 minute, the diseased creature’s skin becomes translucent and slimy, the creature can’t regain hit points unless it is underwater, and the disease can be removed only by heal or another disease-curing spell of 6th level or higher. When the creature is outside a body of water, it takes 6 (1d12) acid damage every 10 minutes unless moisture is applied to the skin before 10 minutes have passed. Tail. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft. one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage. Enslave (3/Day). The aboleth targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed by the aboleth until the aboleth dies or until it is on a different plane of existence from the target. The charmed target is under the aboleth’s control and can’t take reactions, and the aboleth and the target can communicate telepathically with each other over any distance. Whenever the charmed target takes damage, the target can repeat the saving throw. On a success, the effect ends. No more than once every 24 hours, the target can also repeat the saving throw when it is at least 1 mile away from the aboleth.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The aboleth can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The aboleth regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Detect. The aboleth makes a Wisdom (Perception) check. Tail Swipe. The aboleth makes one tail attack. Psychic Drain (Costs 2 Actions). One creature charmed by the aboleth takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage, and the aboleth regains hit points equal to the damage the creature takes.

A creature that isn’t surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the basilisk sees its reflection within 30 feet of it in bright light, it mistakes itself for a rival and targets itself with its gaze.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The behir makes two attacks: one with its bite and one to constrict. Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage. Constrict. Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Large or smaller creature. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage. The target is grappled (escape DC 14) if the behir isn’t already constricting a creature, and the target is restrained until this grapple ends. Lightning Breath (Recharge 5–6). The behir exhales a line of lightning that is 20 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 66 (12d10) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Swallow. The behir makes one bite attack against a Medium or smaller target it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is also swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the behir, and it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the behir’s turns. A behir can have only one creature swallowed at a time. If the behir takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from the swallowed creature, the behir must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls prone in a space within 10 feet of the behir. If the behir dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 15 feet of movement, exiting prone.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Acid Absorption. Whenever the golem is subjected to acid damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of hit points equal to the acid damage dealt. Berserk. Whenever the golem starts its turn with 60 hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points. Immutable Form. The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form. gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The golem makes two slam attacks. Slam. Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage. The target dies if this attack reduces its hit point maximum to 0. The reduction lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. Haste (Recharge 5–6). Until the end of its next turn, the golem magically gains a +2 bonus to its AC, has advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and can use its slam attack as a bonus action.

While attached to the target, the darkmantle can attack no other creature except the target but has advantage on its attack rolls. A creature can detach the darkmantle by making a successful DC 11 Strength check as an action. On its turn, the darkmantle can detach itself from the target by using 5 feet of movement. Darkness Aura (1/Day). A 15-foot radius of magical darkness extends out from the darkmantle, moves with it, and spreads around corners. The darkness lasts as long as the darkmantle maintains concentration, up to 10 minutes (as if concentrating on a spell). Darkvision can’t penetrate this darkness, and no natural light can illuminate it. If any of the darkness overlaps with an area of light created by a spell of 2nd level or lower, the spell creating the light is dispelled.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Heated Body. A creature that touches the remorhaz or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 10 (3d6) fire damage.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 40 (6d10 + 7) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) fire damage. If the target is a creature, it is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the remorhaz can’t bite another target. Swallow. The remorhaz makes one bite attack against a Medium or smaller creature it is grappling. If the attack hits, that creature takes the bite’s damage and is swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the remorhaz, and it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the remorhaz’s turns. If the remorhaz takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the remorhaz must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet of the remorhaz. If the remorhaz dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse using 15 feet of movement, exiting prone.

lines: This immense predator can clamp one foe in its jaws while sweeping at another with its tail.

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Swallow. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., against one Huge or smaller creature the regisaur has grappled. A hit swallows the creature and ends the grapple. If a swallowed creature deals 25 or more damage to the regisaur in one turn, the regisaur makes a DC 16 Constitution save at the end of that turn. gm.title: Description
lines: A jewel-bright cloaker waits on furniture for a suitable host. It feeds by mending wounds, and its glow draws unwanted eyes.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC components −1 size, +3 Dex, +5 natural. Touch AC 12, flat-footed AC 14. Base attack +4. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. Fort +9, Ref +5, Will +7. Standard treasure.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Attach +8 melee touch (no damage).
Full attack. Attach +8 melee touch (no damage) and bite +3 melee (1d4 + 2), as printed.
Color Spray (Su). Release a burst that works like color spray from a 6th-level sorcerer. DC 16 Will negates.
Attach (Su). If the spray stuns or knocks out a human-shaped living creature at least one size smaller, attempt a touch attack to make it a host.
Hit Point Drain (Su). As a free action each round, heal up to 5 HP of damage to either the cloaker or its host. For every 2 HP it heals on the host, it feeds on 1 HP of that damage. When it heals itself from its host, the host takes 2 damage for each HP the cloaker regains. It cannot heal damage it inflicted. If it fails to feed on at least 1 HP of damage in a day, it takes 1 damage.

gm.title: Host and vulnerabilities
lines: It detaches if the host dies, if either the host or the cloaker receives magical healing, or if it goes four days without feeding. A DC 15 Strength check can tear it free. Both make DC 14 Fortitude saves or die, and a surviving host is stunned for 1d8 minutes. The cloaker loses 1 HD per week without a host and recovers 1 HD per day of feeding on a new host. Magical darkness deals 1 damage per round to the cloaker. Healing magic applied to the cloaker deals the amount that would be healed to both it and its host.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide +12, Listen +11, Move Silently +12, Spot +11. Its glow grants observers a +10 circumstance bonus to Spot it except in very bright light. Feats: Alertness, Improved Initiative.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Underground. Solitary. Usually chaotic neutral. Advancement 7–9 HD (Large), 10–18 HD (Huge).

gm.title: Shared dread cloaker rules
lines:
Printed source. Cloaker, Dread, p. 51.
Damage reduction (Su). A cloaker draped around its host shares its damage reduction against physical attacks other than area attacks.
Engulf (Ex). As a standard action, the cloaker envelops a creature at least one size category smaller. Its host is engulfed automatically. Any other target requires a successful grapple check without provoking an attack of opportunity. The target is pinned. A cloaker without a host gains +4 to bite the engulfed creature.
Split damage from attacks that hit an engulfing cloaker equally between it and its victim. Area spells deal full damage to both. A shadow or undead cloaker can still strike other targets with its tail while engulfing a creature.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The stat block gives both 6d8 + 20 and 35 HP. Use its listed HP for the printed specimen. The Base Attack/Grapple row gives +4 alone.

gm.title: Description
lines: Followers of Lolth built these spiderlike constructs to take demons alive. They also send retrievers after other creatures or objects that must come back intact.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Understands Abyssal, Elvish, and Undercommon but cannot speak.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Necrotic, poison, psychic. Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not adamantine.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Faultless Tracker. The master assigns one quarry at a time. It can be a specific creature or object the master knows personally, or a type of creature or object the master has seen. On the same plane as its quarry, the retriever knows the direction and distance to it. The retriever always knows its master's location.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Foreleg attacks and use Force Beam or Paralyzing Beam if available.
Foreleg. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d8 + 6) slashing damage.
Force Beam. One creature the retriever can see within 60 ft. makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. It takes 27 (5d10) force damage on a failure or half on a success.
Paralyzing Beam (Recharge 5–6). One creature the retriever can see within 60 ft. makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure it is paralyzed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. During its movement, the retriever can pick up a creature paralyzed this way if it is Medium or smaller. The retriever can then carry the creature while walking or climbing at full speed.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Wisdom (spell save DC 13). Material components are waived.
3/day each. Web, Plane Shift. Plane Shift carries only the retriever and up to one incapacitated creature, which counts as willing for the spell.

gm.title: Description
lines: A Void predator opens unstable rifts with its oversized claws. It looks for vulnerable worlds and may open a rift for someone whose aims it shares.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 17, Stealth 13. Resistant to necrotic damage and to Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned. Darkvision 60 ft. Languages Common and Void Speech.

lines: Str +8, Dex +3, Con +5, Int +3, Wis +7, Cha +2

gm.title: Traits
lines: Aberrant Resilience. Resistance to Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned. Advantage on saves against spells or effects that change its form.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Void Claw or four Void Bolt attacks. Replace two attacks with Black Gate if it is available. After two Void Claw hits on the same creature, it has disadvantage on its next save against this ripper’s Black Gate within 1 minute.
Void Claw. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. A Medium or smaller creature is Grappled (escape DC 16). Each of the two claws can hold one target.
Void Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit 17 (4d6 + 3) necrotic damage.
Black Gate (recharge 6). Open a rift in an unoccupied visible space within 120 ft. It lasts 1 minute or until the ripper dies or spends an action closing it. Any other creature starting its turn within 20 ft. must pass a DC 16 Strength save or be drawn into a Void demiplane. A banished creature can spend its action to make a DC 16 Intelligence save. On success it reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the gate.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Reality Skip. The ripper teleports itself or one visible creature within 30 ft., along with worn or carried equipment, up to 30 ft. to an unoccupied space the ripper can see. An unwilling target can avoid this with a DC 16 Wisdom save.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

Destroying a tendril deals no damage to the roper, which can extrude a replacement tendril on its next turn. lines:

Etherealness. The ghost crosses between the Material and Ethereal Planes. Creatures on either side can see it across the boundary while it is in the Border Ethereal, and effects cannot cross between the planes.

The ghost cannot be targeted except by effects that turn undead. It retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being Charmed and Frightened. It uses the host's other statistics without gaining its knowledge, class features, or proficiencies.
The possession ends if the host drops to 0 HP, the ghost ends it as a bonus action, it is turned, or magic such as Dispel Evil and Good forces it out. The ghost reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the host. After a successful save or after the possession ends, the host is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours.

gm.title: Death House Possession
lines:
When Rose possesses a player character in Death House, the player retains control and takes on this flaw. I want to be in charge and resent being told what to do. The character will not willingly leave the house or its dungeon.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: MCDM demon soul rules
lines:
Soul count. Use the printed starting total or roll the listed dice. Souls spent on a feature are deducted from the total. A demon can accumulate souls without a maximum.
Soul Devourer. When the demon drops a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure, the demon consumes its soul, adds 1 to its soul count, and the creature dies. Only Wish can restore it to life.
Lethe. At 0 souls, the demon has advantage on attacks and disadvantage on saving throws, and its Intelligence is 3. On each turn it must use its movement to get as close as possible to the nearest creature it senses with Soulsight. If able, it must then use its action to attack that creature and attempt to kill it. It can pursue no other goal until its soul count rises.
Soulsight. Within the creature’s listed radius, it perceives creatures other than Constructs and Undead. This counts as seeing them for its features. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.

gm.title: Description
lines: Mobs of these demons roam the Abyss and surround intruders. Their bites carry a disease that can turn a dying victim into a manes.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Immobilizing Fear. A creature other than a demon that starts its turn within 30 ft. of one or more rutterkins makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. It has disadvantage if six or more rutterkins are within that range. On a failure the creature is frightened of the rutterkins for 1 minute and restrained while frightened this way. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. Any successful save grants immunity to every rutterkin's Immobilizing Fear for 24 hours.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 12 (3d6 + 2) piercing damage. A creature hit makes a DC 13 Constitution save against disease or becomes poisoned. It can repeat the save at the end of each long rest, ending the effect on a success. If it drops to 0 HP while poisoned by the bite, it dies and immediately becomes a living Manes. Only Wish can reverse the transformation.

gm.title: Description
lines: This effigy houses the spirit of an eidolon that guards a sacred site. The effigy becomes a construct while the eidolon animates it.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Large construct, shares the eidolon's alignment

gm.title: Languages
lines: The languages the Eidolon knew in life.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Acid, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
False Appearance. The statue has advantage on its initiative roll if it is motionless when combat starts. A creature that has never seen the statue move or act needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to recognize it as a creature.
Ghostly Inhabitant. The eidolon leaves if the statue drops to 0 HP, if the eidolon spends a bonus action to move out, or if an effect turns or forces it out, such as Dispel Evil and Good. It appears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the statue.
Inert. The statue is an object while empty.
Unusual Nature. The statue needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

Multiattack. Make two Slam or Rock attacks in any combination.

gm.title: Sacred animation mechanics
lines: When an Eidolon enters the statue's space, it can animate the statue with Sacred Animation (Recharge 5–6). The eidolon uses this stat block instead of its own until it leaves. Page 114 lists CR and XP only for the Eidolon.

gm.title: Sacrament of the Falling Fire
lines: A one-hour rite in the Deep Haze, range 30 ft. Up to twelve willing, faithful Humanoids each use a 100 gp delerium fragment and become sanctified. Each confronts a hostile Shadow or, if the GM judges that the participant harbors substantial anger, fear or hatred, a Wraith. While faithful, they have advantage on saves against Charmed or Frightened, resist necrotic and radiant damage, and are immune to contamination. If they die, their soul enters the fragment and cannot be raised while it remains there.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Traits

gm.title: Actions
lines:

gm.title: Description
lines: This sapphire dragon draws power from its other lives. Its breath deals force damage, and its awakened form can move enemies with Mass Telekinesis.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Gem Awakening (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 hit points, it instead resets to 400 hit points, recharges Breath Weapon and recovers all spent Legendary Resistance uses. It can use Mass Telekinesis for the next hour. Defeating it after Gem Awakening grants an extra 90,000 XP, or 180,000 XP total.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The greatwyrm can turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing damage plus 16 (3d10) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d8 + 9) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 19) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can grapple only one creature this way at a time.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. A failure deals 71 (11d12) force damage and knocks the creature prone. A success halves the damage. The creature’s speed is 0 until the end of its next turn on either result.
Mass Telekinesis (Gem Awakening Only, Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Choose any number of visible creatures or objects within 120 ft., each weighing at most 4,000 lb. Worn or carried objects are ineligible. Each chosen creature must pass a DC 26 Strength save or be restrained in the greatwyrm’s grip. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, escaping on a success. At the end of each of the greatwyrm’s turns, it can move each target still in its grip up to 60 ft. in any direction, within 120 ft. of itself. It can also deal 45 (7d12) force damage to each restrained creature it chooses.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 26, +18 to hit) and requiring no components. Dispel Magic, Forcecage, Plane Shift, Reverse Gravity and Time Stop are each usable once per day.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Change Shape. Magically take the shape of a Small or Medium creature. Only size changes. The transformation ends when the greatwyrm drops to 0 hit points or spends a bonus action to end it.
Psychic Step. Magically teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 ft.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The greatwyrm has three legendary actions and recovers spent actions at the start of its turn. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Claw (1 action). Make one Claw attack.
Psionics (2 actions). Use Psychic Step or Spellcasting.
Psychic Beam (3 actions). Each creature in a 90-ft. line 10 ft. wide makes a DC 26 Intelligence save, taking 27 (5d10) psychic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

lines: Fizban’s customization guidance (p. 34) allows changes to languages, skill and tool proficiencies, senses, and traits. Its examples include Change Shape, Flyby, Mimicry, Rejuvenation and Tunneler.

lines: Rare beds, appearing 2d4, active by day. Neutral. Intelligence 2–4. Steady morale 11–12. No treasure or magic resistance.

lines: The plants have no direct attack. Assign a regional Legacy to each bed, offensive or defensive. After the bed uses a Legacy three times in a day, choose a different random Legacy for its next use. The bed can keep using powers while any plant survives. gm.title: Description
lines: The lone survivor of an assassins’ guild took its name as his own. Bound to the Ring of Scarlet Shadows, he wants to become a god of death.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Studded leather. Saving throws Dex +10, Int +4, Wis +8. Acrobatics +10, Perception +8, Sleight of Hand +10, Stealth +13. Resists necrotic damage. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 18. Speaks Common and Draconic.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: p. 384. Villain party action, p. 382. Soulbinder items and curse, pp. 380–381.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Assassinate. On Scarlet's first turn, his attacks have advantage against creatures that have yet to act. His first hit against a surprised creature is a critical hit.
Sneak Attack (1/turn). A weapon hit deals 14 (4d6) extra damage if he has advantage. It also qualifies when an ally who can act is within 5 ft. of the target and Scarlet lacks disadvantage.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Shadow Blade attacks or three bow attacks. Use the listed Longbow profile for the bow attacks.
Shadow Blade. Melee weapon attack +10, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d6 + 7) necrotic damage. A target hit by two or more Shadow Blade attacks in one turn makes a DC 18 Wisdom save or is Blinded through the end of its next turn.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack +10, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing damage.
Razor Garrote. Melee weapon attack +10, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) slashing damage. A Medium or smaller creature is Grappled, escape DC 17. Until free, it is Restrained and takes 22 (5d8) slashing damage at the start of its turns. Scarlet can attack only that target during the grapple.
Umbral Breath (recharge 6). Creatures in a 30-ft. cone make DC 18 Dexterity saves. A failure deals 28 (8d6) necrotic damage and leaves the creature Frightened of Scarlet for 1 minute, with a repeat save at the end of each turn. Success halves damage and avoids Frightened.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Cunning Action. Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Soulbinders. The party can use one villain party action per round, after an enemy's turn. Each action is available once per encounter, in any order. The member taking it must be present and able to act.
Action 5, Shadow Shift. Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible unoccupied space, then make one Shadow Blade or Razor Garrote attack with advantage. Any hit is critical.

gm.title: Recoverable Magic Item
lines:
Ring of Scarlet Shadows. Very rare. Attunement required. The wearer gains darkvision to 60 ft. or adds 60 ft. to an existing range, and has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide. A bonus action extends or dismisses a shadow blade from the ring hand. It works as a shortsword dealing necrotic damage. While extended, it cannot be dropped and the hand cannot hold anything else.
Cursed Sentience. The item uses its Soulbinder's alignment, mental ability scores, and languages. It hears and sees in darkness within 60 ft. and can speak to its wearer telepathically. Break attunement with Remove Curse or equivalent magic. After seven days attuned and every 24 hours after that, make a DC 18 Wisdom save. Each failure reduces Wisdom by 1 while attuned. On the third failure, the Soulbinder takes control and changes the wearer's body, statistics, and equipment to match its own. The wearer remains aware. Breaking attunement restores the body and control. The Soulbinder returns to the item when attunement ends or the body dies. After 1d6 + 12 months of possession, the victim's soul and body are destroyed. The full group ritual for permanently lifting the curse is on p. 382.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed Multiattack mentions a Shortbow, but the only bow statistics provided are for a Longbow. This summary uses that listed attack.

gm.title: Description
lines: The hungry, 50-foot scion carries a whole tree as a club. A settlement can prosper for centuries on the slopes of its sleeping cradle.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Great Tree Club attack and two Slam attacks, or make three Boulder attacks.
Great Tree Club. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 30 (4d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must make a DC 23 Strength save. On a failure, the scion pushes it straight away horizontally by up to 100 ft. and knocks it prone.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (4d8 + 8) force damage.
Boulder. Ranged weapon attack, +15 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 27 (3d12 + 8) bludgeoning damage.
Inhale (Recharge 5–6). Each Huge or smaller creature in a 120-ft. line that is 15 ft. wide must make a DC 23 Strength save. On a failure, the scion pulls it up to 120 ft. straight toward itself and swallows it. The scion can hold up to two creatures at a time. They are restrained, have total cover against attacks and other effects originating outside the scion, and take 24 (7d6) force damage at the start of each of the scion’s turns. If one creature inside deals at least 60 damage to the scion in a single turn, the scion must pass a DC 17 Constitution save at that turn’s end or regurgitate every swallowed creature. Each lands prone in a space within 10 ft. of the scion. If the scion dies, swallowed creatures cease to be restrained and can spend 15 ft. of movement to escape its corpse, exiting prone.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Earth-Shaking Movement. Move up to the scion’s speed, then send a shock wave through the ground in a 60-ft.-radius circle centered on the scion. Each concentrating creature on the ground there loses concentration unless it makes a DC 23 Constitution save.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Feed. Immediately after taking damage while it has a creature swallowed, the scion deals 10 (3d6) force damage to each swallowed creature and regains 10 HP.

gm.title: Cradle encounter
lines: The Cradle of the Hill Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Abundant Food. Crops and livestock grow and reproduce unusually fast within 6 miles.
Empowered Hill Giants. Hill giants within 1,000 ft. gain +7 to attack and damage rolls.
Farming Weather. Within 6 miles the weather stays warm and sunny, with occasional showers that favor farming.
On the scion’s death, all of these effects end immediately.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants, pp. 164–165. The scion’s stat block is on p. 165.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lanky, 75-foot giant with a weapon made of dense cloud. It turns fighting creatures against one another for its own amusement.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Flyby. Flying out of an enemy’s reach does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Legendary Resistance (6/Day). When the scion fails a save, it can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. The scion makes saves against spells and other magical effects with advantage.
Siege Monster. The scion deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one attack with Cloud Morningstar or Wind Javelin, then two Slam attacks.
Cloud Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) force damage plus 22 (4d10) thunder damage.
Wind Javelin. Ranged weapon attack, +18 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 42 (5d12 + 10) thunder damage. The target falls prone unless it makes a DC 26 Strength save.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d8 + 10) force damage.
Thunderous Vortex (Recharge 5–6). Center a 60-ft.-radius sphere of magical wind on a visible point within 120 ft. Each creature in it must make a DC 24 Strength save or be pulled straight toward the center, stopping in the nearest unoccupied space to that point. Then the scion releases thunder in a 30-ft.-radius sphere at that same point. Each creature in the smaller sphere takes 52 (8d12) thunder damage and must pass a DC 24 Constitution save or be stunned until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Fog of Deception. Center a 30-ft.-radius magical cloud on a visible point within 90 ft. Each creature in the cloud makes a DC 24 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is charmed until the end of its next turn. It must use its action for a melee attack against another creature the scion chooses. If none is within reach, it instead makes a ranged attack against a creature the scion chooses, throwing its weapon if necessary. Success makes the creature immune to this scion’s Fog of Deception for 24 hours.

gm.title: Cradle encounter
lines: The Cradle of the Cloud Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Compulsory Offering. The first time a sapient creature comes within 6 miles, it makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, it feels compelled to hide an offering worth at least 5 gp. Cloud giants within 6 miles of the cradle or scion immediately sense where the gift is. A creature can be affected by the compulsion only once.
Empowered Cloud Giants. Cloud giants within 1,000 ft. gain +8 to attack and damage rolls.
Mischievous Whispers. Within 1 mile, the wind carries indistinct whispers. A creature with Intelligence 5 or higher takes them as directions for a prank it can play on someone else.
On the scion’s death, all of these effects end immediately.

gm.title: Bonus actions

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Hailstone. Ranged weapon attack, +18 to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. A hit deals 32 (4d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) cold damage. The target falls prone unless it passes a DC 26 Strength save.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 36 (4d12 + 10) force damage.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Vengeful Storm (Recharge 6). Create a heavily obscuring storm cloud in a 30-ft.-radius, 10-ft.-tall cylinder centered within 120 ft. It lasts 1 minute or until the scion dies or conjures a new cloud. When it appears, and as a bonus action on later turns, the scion can move the cloud up to 30 ft. and cause one effect below in a 30-ft.-radius, 120-ft.-high cylinder directly beneath it. It cannot choose the same effect two rounds in a row.
Acid Rain. Each creature in the cylinder makes a DC 25 Constitution save. On a failure, acid coats it for 1 minute or until a creature uses an action to remove the acid from itself or another creature. A coated creature takes 26 (4d12) acid damage at the start of each of its turns.
Freezing Storm. Each creature in the cylinder makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 28 (8d6) cold damage and reduces its speed to 0 for 1 minute. The creature, or another creature within reach, can use an action to break away the ice and end the effect.
Lightning Bolts. Each creature in the cylinder makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 18 (4d8) lightning damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Cradle encounter
lines: The Cradle of the Storm Scion protects the sleeping scion. When the cradle drops to 0 HP, the scion appears immediately in the cradle’s space and uses its initiative count.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Use one or more of these effects around the scion.
Elemental Portals. Two-way portals within 1 mile of the cradle or scion admit elemental creatures. They connect to the Elemental Plane of Air if the scion is in the sky, or the Elemental Plane of Water if it is in the ocean.
Empowered Storm Giants. Storm giants within 1,000 ft. gain +8 to attack and damage rolls.
Extreme Weather. Within 1 mile, the weather swings sharply from day to day, from bright sunshine to punishing hail.
On the scion’s death, all of these effects end immediately.

lines:

gm.title: Hag Eye
lines: A coven can have one Hag Eye. A coven member on the same plane can spend an action to see through it. The eye has AC 10, 1 HP, and darkvision 60 ft. gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception +4, Stealth +5. Passive Perception 14. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. It can breathe air and water.
Keen Smell. It has Advantage on Perception checks that use smell.
Pack Tactics. It attacks with Advantage if an ally within 5 ft. of the target is not Incapacitated.
Swimming Leap. After swimming at least 10 ft. it can long jump up to 25 ft. out of or across the water.

Claw. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage.
