gm.title: Description
lines: A wild predator made from several creatures. In Theros, unstable magic and portals to Nyx can spawn new chimeras near one another.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Spell Turning. The chimera has advantage on saves against spells that target it alone. If it succeeds against a spell of 4th level or lower, the spell affects the caster instead.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Claws attack, one Head attack, and one Tail attack. If the breath weapon has recharged, it can replace Claws or Head.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage on a hit.
Head. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 10 (1d12 + 4) piercing damage on a hit.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Deal 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage on a hit.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Deal 32 (5d12) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Customizing a chimera
lines: Use the base configuration or roll one d4 on each customization table you want to use. Apply the chosen body adjustments and replace the corresponding breath, head, or tail option. Claws remain available in every configuration. Choose which result to keep if two conflict.

gm.title: Body Composition (d4)
lines:
1. Plains Creature. Give it a large lowland body such as a bear or bull. Remove its wings and fly speed. It gains resistance to cold and fire damage.
2. Coast Creature. Give it a coastal or aquatic body such as a heron or shark. It gains a swim speed equal to its walking speed and can breathe air and water.
3. Mountain Creature. Give it a mountain creature’s body such as a ram or dragon. It can fly out of an enemy’s reach without provoking an opportunity attack.
4. Swamp Creature. Give it a swamp or cave creature’s body such as a giant lizard or spider. It gains a climb speed equal to its walking speed and can climb hard surfaces and ceilings without an ability check.

gm.title: Head Attacks (d4)
lines:
1. Bull Horns. If it moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hits with Head on that turn, deal an extra 7 (2d6) piercing damage. A creature hit must also pass a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
2. Shark Bite. Make Head attacks with advantage against creatures below their maximum hit points.
3. Unicorn Horn. Head is magical and deals an extra 4 (1d8) radiant damage.
4. Cockatrice Beak. A creature hit with Head must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or become restrained. It repeats the save at the end of its next turn. A success ends the restraint. A failure petrifies it for 24 hours.

gm.title: Breath Weapons (d4)
lines:
All four alternatives recharge on 5–6.
1. Lightning Breath. Each creature in a line 60 ft. long and 5 ft. wide makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. Deal 36 (8d8) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.
2. Tidal Wave Breath. Each creature in a line 60 ft. long and 5 ft. wide makes a DC 15 Dexterity save. A failure deals 27 (5d10) acid damage and knocks the creature prone. A success halves the damage and leaves it standing.
3. Venom Spray. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or become poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned this way, it takes 35 (10d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
4. Necrotic Breath. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or take 31 (7d8) necrotic damage and lose the ability to regain hit points through the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Tail Attacks (d4)
lines:
1. Venomous Tail. The tail deals piercing damage. A creature hit by Tail must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or become poisoned for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
2. Perplexing Tail. Replace the tail with a second head. Multiattack uses Claws and two Head attacks. Use the Head Attacks table to determine the added head. The breath substitution remains available.
3. Shark Tail. When Tail hits a creature, the fin also pushes it up to 10 ft. away.
4. Constricting Tail. Tail also grapples a Large or smaller creature it hits (escape DC 15). That creature is restrained while grappled and the tail stays occupied until it escapes or is released.

lines: The ghost of a young boy in a hooded coat who clutches a doll.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Damage resistances: acid, fire, lightning, thunder, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks. Damage immunities: cold, necrotic, poison. Condition immunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. Languages: Common.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Ethereal Sight. The ghost sees 60 ft. from the Material Plane into the Ethereal Plane and the same distance in the reverse direction.
Incorporeal Movement. The ghost treats creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain when moving through them. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Reformation. A ghost reduced to 0 HP can reform at the next dawn. Laying its remains in the matching family crypt puts it to rest and ends any possession.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Withering Touch. Melee weapon attack +5, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 17 (4d6 + 3) necrotic damage.
Etherealness. The ghost crosses between the Material and Ethereal Planes. Creatures on either side can see it across the boundary while it is in the Border Ethereal, and effects cannot cross between the planes.
Possession (Recharge 6). Choose one visible humanoid within 5 ft. The humanoid must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma save or the ghost disappears into its body. The host remains aware. Normally the host is Incapacitated and the ghost controls its body. Apply the Death House exception below when the host is a player character. The ghost cannot be targeted except by effects that turn undead. It retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being Charmed and Frightened. It uses the host's other statistics without gaining its knowledge, class features, or proficiencies.
The possession ends if the host drops to 0 HP, the ghost ends it as a bonus action, it is turned, or magic such as Dispel Evil and Good forces it out. The ghost reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the host. After a successful save or after the possession ends, the host is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours.

gm.title: Death House Possession
lines:
When Thorn possesses a player character in Death House, the player retains control and takes on this flaw. Everything frightens me, and I cry when things go wrong. The character will not willingly leave the house or its dungeon.
A creature can spend an action and succeed on a DC 11 Charisma (Intimidation) check to drive Thorn out. Laying the children to rest in both crypts grants each character Inspiration.

gm.title: Encounter
lines: Disturbing the children's dollhouse or toy chest summons the ghosts. They fight in self-defense and try to possess people who attempt to leave. Rose can point the group toward the secret attic door. Characters who search the dollhouse afterward have Advantage on Perception checks to find secret doors.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Rules source: Curse of Strahd, Death House pp. 217–218. Base Ghost rules from Monster Manual (2014), p. 147.

lines: Saving throws Con +9, Wis +9. Resists cold and lightning damage and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from mundane attacks. gm.title: Traits
lines:
Corpse Retreat (1/day). When reduced to 0 HP, the thornblood drops to 1 HP instead and withdraws into the Medium Humanoid corpse it grew from. It becomes immune to all damage through the end of its next turn. It is Medium, both speeds become 60 ft., and it loses access to Throttle and Overgrowth until it finishes a long rest.
Overgrowth. The thornblood passes through gaps as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing. It can share spaces with other creatures.
Supernatural Resistance. The thornblood has advantage on saves against powers, spells, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make four attacks in any combination of Vinerip and Throttle.
Vinerip. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, 30-ft. reach, one target. Hit 20 (4d6 + 6) bludgeoning plus 11 (2d10) piercing damage. Pull the target up to 30 ft. closer.
Throttle. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, 0-ft. reach, one target in the thornblood's space. Hit 20 (4d6 + 6) piercing damage and entangled. The entangled target is Restrained, moves with the thornblood, cannot see beyond its space, and takes 20 (4d6 + 6) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. The target or a creature within 5 ft. of it can use an action to take 20 (4d6 + 6) slashing damage and attempt a DC 20 Strength check, freeing the target on a success.
From Life, Lightning (2/day). Requires at least one entangled creature. Each entangled creature makes a DC 20 Constitution save, taking 55 (10d10) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. Then each enemy within 60 ft. that is not entangled makes a DC 20 Dexterity save, taking 55 (10d10) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn, a Dazed creature chooses only one: move, take an action, or take a bonus action. Becoming Dazed during its turn ends that turn. gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Fury shared rules
lines:
Printed source. Furies, pp. 79–80. The sisters appear together and speak all humanoid languages. They try three times to divert a target from atonement before trying to kill them in public.
Defenses. Damage reduction 15/good. Immune to paralysis, polymorph, and mind-affecting effects.
Scourge. The +3 scourge works like a whip that deals 1d4 lethal damage before modifiers. A Fury may substitute it for her claw attacks. Use the attack and ability damage listed for that sister. Rake (Ex) is +9 melee for 1d4 + 1 damage.
Alter Self (Sp). At will as a standard action, a Fury can take the form of an elderly human woman indefinitely. Caster level 10.
Breath Weapon (Su, 3/day). Fill one adjacent square with foul air. Apply stinking cloud as cast by an 8th-level sorcerer, with a DC 16 Fortitude save.
Find Penitent (Su). Furies can locate a target who seeks redemption at the invitation or embrace stage of corruption. The target cannot hide from them, even with magic.
Gaseous Death (Su). At 0 HP, a Fury and her scourge dissolve into smoke. Surviving sisters continue to fight, though the last survivor tries to flee. If a sister survives, the slain Furies return at full HP after 24 hours. To kill them permanently, all three must die within the same 24 hours and an Innocent must deal the killing blows. Their scourges remain after permanent death.
Weaknesses. A good cleric or a paladin can turn each Fury separately by invoking her true name. A turning attempt cannot destroy, rebuke, or command her. A Fury cannot deliberately harm a good creature except with her breath weapon.

gm.title: Description
lines: Titivilus negotiates on Dispater's behalf. He recruits outsiders to remove rivals and create problems that he can solve to secure his place at court.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that do not use silvered weapons.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When Titivilus fails a save, he can spend one use to succeed.
Magic Resistance. Titivilus has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Regeneration. Titivilus regains 10 hit points at the start of his turn. Taking cold or radiant damage prevents this healing at the start of his next turn. He dies only if he begins his turn at 0 hit points and fails to regenerate.
Ventriloquism. When Titivilus speaks, he can make his voice come from a point he chooses within 60 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Silver Sword attack and use Frightful Word.
Silver Sword. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) force damage with one hand or 9 (1d10 + 4) force damage with two hands, plus 16 (3d10) necrotic damage either way. A creature hit loses maximum hit points equal to half the necrotic damage it takes.
Frightful Word. Choose a visible creature within 10 ft. It must pass a DC 21 Wisdom save or be frightened of Titivilus for 1 minute. On its turns, it must Dash and move away by the safest available route. It can skip the Dash if it has nowhere to move. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Teleport. Titivilus and his worn or carried equipment teleport up to 120 ft. to an unoccupied space he can see.
Twisting Words. Choose a visible creature within 60 ft. It must pass a DC 21 Charisma save or become charmed by Titivilus for 1 minute. If Titivilus damages the charmed creature, it can repeat the save to end the charm. A creature that succeeds on the save gains immunity to his Twisting Words for 24 hours.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Use an action to cast one spell without material components. Charisma is the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 21).
At will. Alter Self, Major Image, Nondetection, Sending, Suggestion.
3/day each. Mislead, Modify Memory.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Titivilus has 3 legendary actions and recovers them at the start of his turn. Spend the stated cost on one option immediately after another creature finishes its turn. He cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using them.
Corrupting Guidance (1 action). Use Twisting Words, or choose a creature within 60 ft. that Titivilus has charmed. On a failed DC 21 Charisma save, he decides how it acts during its next turn.
Teleport (1 action). Use Teleport.
Assault (2 actions). Make one Silver Sword attack or use Frightful Word.

lines: Dispater’s adviser uses a silver sword, deceptive speech and magical misdirection to manipulate enemies.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold. Also bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When Titivilus fails a saving throw, he can succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. Titivilus has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. His weapon attacks are magical.
Regeneration. Titivilus regains 10 hit points at the start of his turn. Cold or radiant damage suppresses this healing at the start of his next turn. He dies only if he starts his turn with 0 hit points and does not regenerate.
Ventriloquism. Whenever Titivilus speaks, he can make his voice come from a point he chooses within 60 ft.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
Titivilus casts with Charisma (spell save DC 21) and needs no material components.
At will. Alter Self, Animate Dead, Bestow Curse, Confusion, Major Image, Modify Memory, Nondetection, Sending, Suggestion.
3/day each. Greater Invisibility (self only), Mislead.
1/day each. Feeblemind, Symbol (discord or sleep only).

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Silver Sword attack and use Frightful Word once.
Silver Sword. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage with two hands. Both grips also deal 16 (3d10) necrotic damage. A creature’s hit point maximum decreases by half the necrotic damage it takes.
Frightful Word. Choose one visible creature within 10 ft. It must succeed on a DC 21 Wisdom save or become frightened of Titivilus for 1 minute. On each turn while frightened this way, the creature must Dash and take the safest route away from him. If no route is available, it does not have to Dash. At the end of each of the target’s turns, it can save again to end the effect.
Teleport. Titivilus magically moves himself and the equipment he wears or carries up to 120 ft. to a visible unoccupied space.
Twisting Words. Choose one visible creature within 60 ft. It must succeed on a DC 21 Charisma save or become charmed by Titivilus for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save if Titivilus damages it. A successful save makes it immune to his Twisting Words for 24 hours.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Titivilus has three legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He can use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Assault (Costs 2 Actions). Make a Silver Sword attack or use Frightful Word.
Corrupting Guidance. Use Twisting Words, or choose one creature within 60 ft. that Titivilus has charmed. That creature makes a DC 21 Charisma save. On a failure, Titivilus decides how the creature acts during its next turn.
Teleport. Use the Teleport action.

lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Berserk. Whenever the golem starts its turn with 40 hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points. The golem’s creator, if within 60 feet of the berserk golem, can try to calm it by speaking firmly and persuasively. The golem must be able to hear its creator, who must take an action to make a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check. If the check succeeds, the golem ceases being berserk. If it takes damage while still at 40 hit points or fewer, the golem might go berserk again. Aversion of Fire. If the golem takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn. Immutable Form. The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form. Lightning Absorption. Whenever the golem is subjected to lightning damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of hit points equal to the lightning damage dealt. Magic Resistance. The golem has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. Magic Weapons. The golem’s weapon attacks are magical.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Mace. Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage. Priests bring the teachings of their gods to the common folk. They are the spiritual leaders of temples and shrines and often hold positions of influence in their communities. Evil priests might work openly under a tyrant, or they might be the leaders of religious sects hidden in the shadows of good society, overseeing depraved rites. A priest typically has one or more acolytes to help with religious ceremonies and other sacred duties.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Gem Awakening (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). When the greatwyrm would drop to 0 hit points, it instead resets to 400 hit points, recharges Breath Weapon and recovers all spent Legendary Resistance uses. It can use Mass Telekinesis for the next hour. Defeating it after Gem Awakening grants an extra 90,000 XP, or 180,000 XP total.
Legendary Resistance (4/day). The greatwyrm can turn a failed save into a success.
Unusual Nature. The greatwyrm needs no food or drink.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing damage plus 16 (3d10) force damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (2d8 + 9) slashing damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 19) and restrained until the grapple ends. The greatwyrm can grapple only one creature this way at a time.
Breath Weapon (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 300-ft. cone makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. A failure deals 71 (11d12) force damage and knocks the creature prone. A success halves the damage. The creature’s speed is 0 until the end of its next turn on either result.
Mass Telekinesis (Gem Awakening Only, Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Choose any number of visible creatures or objects within 120 ft., each weighing at most 4,000 lb. Worn or carried objects are ineligible. Each chosen creature must pass a DC 26 Strength save or be restrained in the greatwyrm’s grip. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, escaping on a success. At the end of each of the greatwyrm’s turns, it can move each target still in its grip up to 60 ft. in any direction, within 120 ft. of itself. It can also deal 45 (7d12) force damage to each restrained creature it chooses.
Spellcasting (Psionics). As an action, cast one spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 26, +18 to hit) and requiring no components. Dispel Magic, Forcecage, Plane Shift, Reverse Gravity and Time Stop are each usable once per day.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saves Con +8, Wis +5, Cha +7. Intimidation +7, Perception +5. Darkvision 120 ft., Soulsight 30 ft., passive Perception 15. Abyssal and Common. Telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Slam attacks and one Many Maws attack.
Slam. Melee weapon attack +8, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 15) and remains Restrained until the grapple ends. The tormenauk can hold up to two targets this way.
Many Maws. Melee weapon attack +8, reach 5 ft., one target Grappled by the tormenauk. Hit 21 (3d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Agony Wail (1 soul). Each creature within 30 ft. that can hear the tormenauk makes a DC 15 Wisdom save, taking 35 (10d6) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success. Creatures that knew the owner of the spent soul have disadvantage on that save.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Share Agony (1 soul). When the tormenauk takes damage, choose a creature it can see within 30 ft. The creature makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure it takes psychic damage equal to the triggering damage the tormenauk took, or half on a success.

gm.title: MCDM demon soul rules
lines:
Soul count. Use the printed starting total or roll the listed dice. Souls spent on a feature are deducted from the total. A demon can accumulate souls without a maximum.
Soul Devourer. When the demon drops a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure, the demon consumes its soul, adds 1 to its soul count, and the creature dies. Only Wish can restore it to life.
Lethe. At 0 souls, the demon has advantage on attacks and disadvantage on saving throws, and its Intelligence is 3. On each turn it must use its movement to get as close as possible to the nearest creature it senses with Soulsight. If able, it must then use its action to attack that creature and attempt to kill it. It can pursue no other goal until its soul count rises.
Soulsight. Within the creature’s listed radius, it perceives creatures other than Constructs and Undead. This counts as seeing them for its features. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.

gm.title: Description
lines: A shelled coastal humanoid. In a group, the front line withdraws into its shells while the rear line shoots, then emerges when the volleys stop.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Forests and beaches. Uncommon. Tribe. Active by day. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–10. Treasure K. Any alignment. Appearing 2d6. No magic resistance. Height 5–7 feet. Morale 17–18.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws or weapon. Make two claw attacks for 1d4 each or use a weapon. Some tortles have learned a bite that deals 1d6. Favored weapons include short bows, staves, long swords, and flails.
Shell withdrawal. Take no other action that round. While withdrawn, use AC 1 and add +4 to all saves, including saves against mental attacks. The tortle cannot move, attack, or see, but it can hear and smell. Gaze attacks and other effects that require the target to see fail against it while withdrawn.

gm.title: Senses and swimming
lines: Infravision and underwater vision extend 60 feet. It has the Swimming nonweapon proficiency. Buoyancy keeps it afloat even in bogs, quicksand, and mud. It holds its breath for 10 turns. It speaks Tortle and usually Common or another local language.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: Tortles acquire Legacies and need cinnabryl to ward off Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: An opalescent snail chews through barriers and leaves false paths in the Labyrinth. Skilled handlers sometimes train one as a mount for passing through magical wards.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 11, Stealth 10. Resistant to Exhaustion and Frightened. Immune to force damage. Keensense 60 ft. No languages.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +3, Dex +0, Con +3, Int -3, Wis +1, Cha -1

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Dispelling Slime. When the snail deals force damage to a creature under a magical effect, there is a 25% chance to end that effect as Dispel Magic without an ability check. Standing on or chewing a magic item other than an artifact for 1 minute gives a 10% chance of suppressing the item’s magic for 24 hours, disabling activation. A sentient item keeps its awareness and normal means of communication.
Monstrosity Resilience. Resistance to Exhaustion and Frightened.
Rainbow Ward. A creature within 30 ft. that relies on sight has disadvantage on attack rolls against the snail.
Path Maker. At the end of its turn, the snail can deal 9 (2d8) force damage to an object or structure sharing its space, ignoring any damage threshold. Magical barriers such as Wall of Force count as difficult terrain for it. It suffers no other penalties from moving through or starting its turn in a magical barrier’s space.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Slam or Force Spit attacks.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning plus 4 (1d8) force damage.
Force Spit. Ranged weapon attack, +2 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d8) force damage.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Energy Absorption. When the snail takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, it can halve it and deal force damage equal to the resulting amount to each creature it chooses within 5 ft.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Small or Medium humanoid, any alignment

gm.title: Traits
lines:

Unarmored Defense. Add the conduit’s Wisdom modifier to AC while it has neither armor nor a shield.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Unarmed Strike attacks.
Unarmed Strike. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. On hitting a creature, the conduit may choose one of the following effects. Each option can be used once per turn.
Incapacitate. The creature makes a DC 15 Constitution save or is incapacitated through the end of the conduit’s next turn.
Push. Move the creature horizontally up to 10 ft. away from the conduit.

gm.title: Reactions
lines:

Deflect Attack. When an attack roll hits the conduit, reduce that attack’s damage to the conduit by 1d10.
Don’t Be There. When the conduit must make a saving throw, it can move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. If the new position puts it out of range or otherwise makes it an invalid target, it avoids the effect entirely.

gm.title: Description
lines: This subterranean ambush predator spreads against floors, walls, and ceilings. It matches the color and texture of stone, earth, or wood and sometimes leaves old bones and treasure in view as bait.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
False Appearance. The trapper has advantage on initiative if it starts combat motionless on a floor, wall, or ceiling. A creature that has never seen it move or act needs a successful DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check to distinguish it from that surface.
Spider Climb. The trapper climbs difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without making an ability check.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Smother. Choose one Large or smaller creature within 10 ft. It must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity save or be grappled (escape DC 14). Until the grapple ends, it is restrained, blinded, and deprived of air. It takes 13 (3d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns. The trapper can smother one creature at a time.

Animate Trees (1/day). Magically animate up to two trees the treant can see within 60 ft. An animated tree uses this Treant stat block. A hero's burial mound whose animated trees resemble questing knights. 6. A hollow that holds the bones of the person who set it on fire.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

lines: A dryad corrupted by a night hag can seize a living tree and attack from inside it. The tree decays while the skinner lives within.

lines:

lines:

lines:

If reduced to 15 HP, the tree dies and the skinner appears within 5 ft. of it or in the nearest unoccupied space. The skinner can also exit as a bonus action to the nearest unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the tree, returning it to object status. After at most three days of occupation, the tree dies.
Squeeze (tree form only). A creature the skinner is Grappling makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure it cannot breathe or cast spells with verbal components until the Grapple ends.

gm.title: Description
lines: After learning that his own father was plotting his death, Treyvan pledged his muscle and telekinesis to the Amethyst Knife. He wants to seize the dukedom that he was denied.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Plate. Saving throws Str +9, Con +7. Athletics +9, Religion +3. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12. Speaks Common and Elvish. Telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Charm Resistant. Advantage on saves to avoid or end Charmed.
Mind Link. The bosses of the Amethyst Knife can speak telepathically with one another across any distance on the same plane.
Telekinetic Bastion. Allies within 20 ft. gain +2 AC and +2 on Dexterity saves. Enemies treat that area as difficult terrain.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Maul attacks. Treyvan can replace one with Telekinetic Throw or Choke if available.
Maul. Melee weapon attack +9, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target can be knocked Prone or pushed up to 10 ft. away, at Treyvan's choice.
Telekinetic Throw. Make a Maul attack with a range of 30 ft. The maul immediately returns after the attack.
Choke (2/day, 5th-order power, concentration). A visible Large or smaller creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. Failure leaves it Restrained for up to 1 minute. It takes 14 (4d6) force damage at the start of its turns and can repeat the save at the end of each turn. The power ends if it gains total cover from Treyvan or moves beyond 30 ft.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Shared Condition. When the creature becomes Blinded, Charmed, Dazed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned, it can transfer the condition and its remaining duration to a willing Amethyst Knife boss within 60 ft. who neither has the condition nor is immune to it. The condition ends for the original creature. This reaction works even while Incapacitated.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Amethyst Knife. The party can use one villain party action per round, after an enemy's turn. Each action is available once per encounter, in any order. The member taking it must be present and able to act.
Action 1, Amethyst Formation. Treyvan can move each willing Amethyst Knife boss he sees within 60 ft. up to 30 ft. in any direction.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: While Dazed, a creature can use only one of its movement, action, or bonus action on its turn. Gaining Dazed ends the turn if it happens during that turn. Extra actions such as Haste or Action Surge still work. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can end the condition.

gm.title: Psionic Powers (MCDM)
lines: Powers have no components and count as supernatural. Antimagic Field, Counterspell, and Dispel Magic do not stop powers. A creature may maintain several different powers at once, up to its proficiency bonus, but cannot concentrate on a spell or another effect at the same time. Failing a concentration save ends all active powers. If a foe provokes an opportunity attack, the creature can use a melee power attack as its reaction instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: This walking Chultan plant grows three large trumpet-shaped flowers in orange, yellow, and red. Each flower attacks in a different way.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Orange Blossom, then Yellow Blossom, then Red Blossom.
Orange Blossom. Choose one creature the frond can see within 5 ft. On a failed DC 11 Constitution save, the target is poisoned for 1 hour and unconscious while poisoned this way. It can repeat the save at the end of every minute, ending the effect on a success.
Yellow Blossom. Choose one creature the frond can see within 5 ft. On a failed DC 11 Dexterity save, corrosive sap coats the target and deals 5 acid damage at the start of each of its turns. Each pint or flask of water poured over it reduces that recurring damage by 1.
Red Blossom. Melee weapon attack, +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 2 (1d4) piercing damage. The target is grappled (escape DC 11). While this grapple lasts, the target takes 5 (2d4) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. The blossom can grapple one target at a time. Another creature within the frond’s reach can use its action to free the target.

gm.title: Encounters
lines: On the trail, a patch of 1d4 fronds passes for harmless plants until it strikes. Around a camp, the fronds creep closer and use Orange Blossom to incapacitate targets before attacking with the others. Three fronds grow in the garden at area 5B of Nangalore.

lines:

gm.title: Special attacks

Deal 2d12 + 15 bludgeoning damage once per target per round. A trampled opponent can make an attack of opportunity at −4, or attempt a DC 28 Reflex save for half. A partially covered larger space permits the −4 attack of opportunity without trampling. If it ends in an illegal space, return it to its most recent legal position or the nearest legal position if closer.

gm.title: Description
lines: A detached troll arm that crawls and lashes out under its parent’s direction.

gm.title: Severing and reattachment
lines:
When the troll takes 15 or more slashing damage from a single instance, roll a d20. On 1–10 no part is severed. On 11–14 it loses a leg if any remain. On 15–18 it loses an arm if any remain. On 19–20 it is decapitated. It survives the decapitation if it can regenerate. If the troll dies after decapitation, its severed head also dies.
A detached part acts on the troll’s initiative with its own movement and action. If the troll finishes a short or long rest before reattaching the part, a replacement grows and the old part dies. The sidebar gives no reattachment action or timing.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Regeneration. The part regains 10 HP at the start of its turn. Acid or fire damage prevents that healing at the start of its next turn. Applying the troll’s Regeneration to the part, it dies when it begins its turn at 0 HP and cannot regenerate.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Claw. Make one Claw attack on the arm’s turn using the parent Troll’s attack. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage. The attack has disadvantage unless the troll can see both the arm and its target.

gm.title: Effects on the troll
lines: Each lost arm removes one Claw attack from the troll’s Multiattack. Losing its head removes Bite, and the body is Blinded unless the head can see it. With one leg missing, halve the troll’s speed. With both legs missing, it falls Prone and can crawl if it has one or both arms. Halve its speed if it has only one arm to crawl with. With no arms or legs left, its speed is 0 and speed bonuses cannot increase it.

lines: Use this procedure only with the Troll (variant). The sidebar gives each part its own AC, HP, movement and any listed attack. It gives no separate size, ability scores, challenge rating or XP. The DM decides how to resolve checks or saves the sidebar leaves unspecified.

gm.title: Loathsome Limbs
lines:
If the troll takes 15 or more slashing damage at once, roll a d20. On 1–10, no part comes off. On 11–14, sever one remaining leg. On 15–18, sever one remaining arm. On 19–20, decapitate it. A decapitated troll dies only if it cannot regenerate. When it dies, its detached head dies too.
Detached parts. Each has AC 13, 10 HP and the troll’s Regeneration. Each acts on the troll’s initiative with its own movement and action. If the troll completes a short or long rest without reattaching the part, it grows a replacement and the detached part dies.
Leg. A detached leg has speed 5 ft. and cannot attack. The troll’s speed halves after losing one leg. With both legs gone, it falls Prone and can crawl if it has arms. With just one arm it crawls at half speed. With no arms or legs its speed is 0 and speed bonuses do not apply.
Arm. A detached arm has speed 5 ft. and makes one Claw attack on its turn. It has disadvantage unless the troll can see both the arm and the target. Each lost arm removes one Claw from the troll’s Multiattack.
Head. The detached head cannot move, retains Keen Smell, and can Bite only a target in its space. The body loses Bite and is Blinded unless its head can see the body.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

lines:

Hearts of the Kraken (mythic trait, recharges after a short or long rest). Upon dropping to 0 hit points, Tromokratis stays alive and conscious as its carapace cracks open. Track four hearts separately, two on the chest, one on the back, and one at the base of the tail. Each heart has AC 22 and 100 hit points. Each is immune to all conditions and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Use ability scores of 10 (+0) for any saving throw a heart must make. After Tromokratis finishes a short or long rest, the carapace seals over its hearts and any destroyed hearts regenerate. Destroy all four hearts to kill it.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). Tromokratis can turn a failed save into a success.
Magic Weapons. Its weapon attacks are magical.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures.
Spell-Resistant Carapace. It has advantage on saves against spells. Spell attack rolls against it have disadvantage.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Pincer, one Tail, and one Tentacle Grasp attack.
Pincer. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Deal 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage on a hit. A creature hit is grappled (escape DC 26) and restrained. Tromokratis can target only that creature with Pincer until the grapple ends.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Deal 23 (3d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage on a hit. A creature hit falls prone.
Tentacle Grasp. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one creature. Deal 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage on a hit and grapple it (escape DC 26). If the creature is still grappled at the end of its next turn, Tromokratis throws it up to 60 ft. in a straight line. The creature lands prone and takes 21 (6d6) bludgeoning damage.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +18 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Deal 29 (3d12 + 10) piercing damage on a hit. If the target is a Large or smaller creature that Tromokratis has grappled, the Bite also swallows it and ends the grapple. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover from attacks and effects outside the kraken, and takes 42 (12d6) acid damage at the start of each of Tromokratis’s turns. If any single swallowed creature deals at least 50 damage to Tromokratis on one turn, the kraken makes a DC 20 Constitution save at that turn’s end. On a failure it regurgitates all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in spaces within 10 ft. If Tromokratis dies, its restraint ends. A swallowed creature can then spend 15 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, emerging prone.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Tromokratis has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. Use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Move (1 action). Move up to half its speed.
Tail (1 action). Make one Tail attack.
Bite (3 actions). Make one Bite attack.

gm.title: Mythic actions
lines:
For 1 hour after Hearts of the Kraken activates, Tromokratis can spend legendary actions on these options while its mythic trait is active.
Rampage (1 action). Make one Tail attack and one Tentacle Grasp attack.
Coral Growth (2 actions). Each creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Deal 13 (3d8) slashing damage on a failure or half on a success. Tromokratis and each of its hearts gain +2 AC until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Mythic encounter
lines: For the optional second phase, use Hearts of the Kraken when the kraken drops to 0 HP. Treat the full encounter as two CR 26 creatures and award 180,000 XP if the party defeats Tromokratis after the hearts were exposed.

Wrath of Mat’Selesnya (Recharge 5–6). Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in the 30-ft. cube there makes a DC 24 Dexterity save. Failure deals 21 (6d6) bludgeoning plus 21 (6d6) slashing damage. Success halves both.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The creature can spend up to three legendary actions, choosing one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn. It regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.
Voice of Harmony (1 action). Make one melee attack with advantage.
Voice of Life (1 action). Grant 20 temporary HP to another visible creature within 120 ft.
Voice of Order (1 action). Cast Dispel Magic.
Chorus of the Conclave (2 actions). Cast Suggestion, spending a daily use.
Awaken Grove Guardians (3 actions). One or two visible trees within 120 ft. uproot and become Awakened Trees for 1 minute or until Trostani ends the effect as a bonus action. They understand Druidic and follow her spoken orders. They cannot speak. In the absence of orders they follow her and Dodge.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The print pairs Strength 19 with a +5 modifier. This profile keeps the printed score and Constrict numbers. The usual modifier for Strength 19 is +4.

gm.title: Roleplaying
lines: Trostani wants every community to join the Conclave. She takes a member’s departure as a betrayal. Her three personalities disagree over how to meet Ravnica’s rising tensions. See p. 251.

gm.title: MCDM demon soul rules
lines:
Soul count. Use the printed starting total or roll the listed dice. Souls spent on a feature are deducted from the total. A demon can accumulate souls without a maximum.
Soul Devourer. When the demon drops a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure, the demon consumes its soul, adds 1 to its soul count, and the creature dies. Only Wish can restore it to life.
Lethe. At 0 souls, the demon has advantage on attacks and disadvantage on saving throws, and its Intelligence is 3. On each turn it must use its movement to get as close as possible to the nearest creature it senses with Soulsight. If able, it must then use its action to attack that creature and attempt to kill it. It can pursue no other goal until its soul count rises.
Soulsight. Within the creature’s listed radius, it perceives creatures other than Constructs and Undead. This counts as seeing them for its features. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one Large or smaller creature. On a hit the target takes 17 (3d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage and is grappled (escape DC 19). While grappled this way, the target is restrained and takes another 17 (3d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. The typhon can hold two creatures this way at once.

gm.title: Description
lines: An ulitharid is a six-tentacled mind flayer that sometimes leaves its colony with followers to found another.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Large aberration (mind flayer), typically lawful evil

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Creature Sense. The ulitharid detects creatures with Intelligence 4 or higher within 2 miles. It learns each creature’s distance, direction, and Intelligence score. Mind Blank, Nondetection, and similar protections block this sense.
Magic Resistance. The ulitharid has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Psionic Hub. An Elder Brain psychically linked to the ulitharid can link to any other creature the ulitharid detects with Creature Sense. That creature’s link ends once it leaves the telepathy range of both. The ulitharid’s link to the Elder Brain persists across any distance on the same plane. More than 5 miles away from the Elder Brain, the ulitharid can end their link at any time without an action.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. A hit deals 27 (4d10 + 5) psychic damage. A Large or smaller target is also grappled (escape DC 14) and must succeed on a DC 17 Intelligence save or be stunned until the grapple ends.
Extract Brain. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one incapacitated Humanoid grappled by the ulitharid. A hit deals 55 (10d10) piercing damage. If this reduces the target to 0 HP, the ulitharid kills it by removing and eating its brain.
Mind Blast (Recharge 5–6). The ulitharid projects magical psychic energy. Each creature in a 60-ft. cone must succeed on a DC 17 Intelligence save or take 31 (4d12 + 5) psychic damage and be stunned for 1 minute. A stunned creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Spellcasting (Psionics)
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 17). No components are needed.
At will. Detect Thoughts, Levitate.
1/day each. Dominate Monster, Feeblemind, Mass Suggestion, Plane Shift (self only), Project Image, Scrying, Telekinesis.

gm.title: Founding a colony
lines: An ulitharid preparing to give up its life can extract its brain using its psionic staff. Its followers plant the brain and staff in its corpse, which dissolves into ichor and helps form the new Elder Brain’s brine pool. A brain from an ulitharid that died naturally is unsuitable.

gm.title: Description
lines: This ragged, foul-smelling cloaker rides a living host until it can drain another victim. It keeps a dead host as a puppet.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC 21 (printed breakdown −1 size, +3 Dex, +7 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 16. Base attack +2. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. (5 ft. with bite). Fort unlisted, Ref +5, Will +7. Hide +12, Listen +11, Spot +11. Alertness, Improved Initiative. Underground. Solitary. Standard treasure. Always chaotic evil. Advancement 6–8 HD (Large), 9–16 HD (Huge).

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Tail slap +8 melee (1d6+5).
Full attack. Tail slap +8 melee (1d6+5) and bite +3 melee (1d4+2). It can use its tail on other creatures while engulfing.
Attach (Su). After engulfing a human-shaped creature at least one size smaller, it attempts to bite. A hit attaches the cloaker, which can allow the host to move freely after it stops struggling. It loses its bite while attached. Death ward protects a creature against attachment and removes an attached cloaker. The cloaker also detaches if it is destroyed or successfully turned.
Forcible removal. Use the Attach procedure: another character makes a DC 15 Strength check to tear the cloaker free. On success the host gains 1d4 negative levels. The cloaker survives and follows its hostless rules.
Energy Drain (Su). When the host touches a living creature, that creature gains 1 negative level. Use a touch attack if the target resists. If the host touches no living creature over 24 hours, the cloaker instead gives the host 1 negative level. Fortitude DC 14 removes each negative level at the normal recovery check.
Create Spawn (Su). A humanoid killed by the drain rises in 24 hours as a zombie without its living abilities. Zombies remain controlled until the cloaker dies. It stays attached to a dead host and controls that host once it rises.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Undead traits and DR 10/magic. Without a host it loses 1 HD each week until destroyed. Once it attaches, it regains 1 HD for each day it feeds.

gm.title: Shared dread cloaker rules
lines:
Printed source. Cloaker, Dread, p. 51.
Damage reduction (Su). A cloaker draped around its host shares its damage reduction against physical attacks other than area attacks.
Engulf (Ex). As a standard action, the cloaker envelops a creature at least one size category smaller. Its host is engulfed automatically. Any other target requires a successful grapple check without provoking an attack of opportunity. The target is pinned. A cloaker without a host gains +4 to bite the engulfed creature.
Split damage from attacks that hit an engulfing cloaker equally between it and its victim. Area spells deal full damage to both. A shadow or undead cloaker can still strike other targets with its tail while engulfing a creature.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed AC breakdown adds to 19, but the total is 21. Use the printed total, touch, and flat-footed values. The stat block omits grapple and Fortitude. If needed, the standard 3.5 statistics yield grapple +11 and Fortitude +1 against effects that apply to undead. The combat paragraph requires DC 17 and says removal kills the cloaker. The detailed Attach ability instead specifies DC 15 and provides rules for a hostless cloaker. Use the Attach procedure as a table ruling.

gm.title: Description
lines: The leafless ruler of a corrupt grove pins travelers under its branches to feed through its roots.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative −2. Printed AC components −2 size, −1 Dex, +13 natural. Touch AC 7, flat-footed AC 21. Base attack +4, grapple +21. Space 10 ft., reach 15 ft. Fort +0, Ref +1, Will +4.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +21 melee (1d6 + 9). Full attack. Two slams +2 melee (1d6 + 9 each) as printed. A full attack deals double damage to an object or structure.
Trample (Ex). 2d12 + 5 damage, Reflex DC 23 for half.
Blood Drain (Ex). On its next turn after pinning a living foe, 1d3 roots attach. Each root drains 1 Constitution each round it maintains the grapple. It cannot move while feeding and takes a full-round action to become mobile again. Break the pin normally or sever every attached root. Each root has AC 15 and 4 HP independent of the treant. Use Ravenloft vampire feeding rules from chapter 5 of the Ravenloft Player’s Handbook for its feeding needs.
Spells. It casts as a 6th-level druid and chooses no spells that employ fire.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Undead traits, damage reduction 10/slashing, and fire vulnerability. It has lost the living treant’s ability to animate trees.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide −10, Intimidate +8, one Knowledge skill +8, Listen +9, Sense Motive +9, Spot +9, Survival +9. Hide has a +16 racial bonus in dead or dying forest. Feats: Cleave, Improved Sunder, Iron Will, Power Attack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any forest. Solitary or with 4–7 dread treants. Always neutral evil. Standard treasure. Advances to 9–17 HD (Huge) or 18–22 HD (Gargantuan).

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The printed full attack is +2 while its single slam is +21. For a consistent table ruling, use +21 for both slams.
The printed AC components do not add to AC 20, and Dexterity 6 gives a −2 modifier rather than the printed −1 in those components. Use the listed total, touch, and flat-footed values.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

Surprise Attack. In the first round, it attacks surprised creatures with advantage and deals an extra 10 (3d6) damage each time one of those attacks hits.

lines:
Intelligence (spell save DC 14), with no material components.
1/day each. Expeditious Retreat, Fog Cloud, Misty Step.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Petrifying Gaze. Choose one visible creature within 60 ft. that can see the medusa’s eyes. It makes a DC 14 Constitution save. Failure by 5 or more petrifies it immediately. Any other failure restrains it as it turns to stone. A restrained creature repeats the save at the end of its next turn. Failure petrifies it and success ends the effect. Greater Restoration or similar magic ends the petrification.

lines: An Undercity Medusa can qualify a group of six or more Golgari for the shared lair actions on p. 236 while they defend their territory. See Golgari Shaman for the actions and regional effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Each creature in the cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage and becoming restrained by hardened rock on a failure. A success halves the damage and prevents the restraint. gm.title: Description
lines: A white unicorn with golden strands in its mane and tail. Its humanoid form is a young knight in white chain mail.

lines: Natural AC 2. In humanoid form the chain mail gives AC 3. Magic resistance 15%. Exceptional intelligence 15–16. Fearless morale 19–20.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Sense true enemies within 240 yards. Both forms are immune to charm, hold and poison, and make other saves as an 11th-level wizard. The white mail vanishes if taken off. The servant must spend one full turn in natural form before the armor can reappear.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Hooves and horn, natural form. Make two hoof attacks at 1d6 damage each and a horn attack at 1d12. The horn attack gets +2 to hit. If the unicorn has 30 feet to build up speed, it can charge with only the horn for 3d12 damage. The horn's touch dispels magic as an 11th-level wizard.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: No bearer is named. Tradition says the servant is granted to a fair and just human or elven maiden. The bearer can sense true enemies and gains the servant's spell immunities while in contact with it.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lion-headed exile from Carceri, with white claws, red scales, and quills for a mane. It sometimes spends a year in the mortal world before returning home.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Common in Carceri and very rare elsewhere. Solitary carnivore. Exceptional intelligence (15–16). Treasure F, R, X. Champion morale (15–16). Height 11–14 feet. 120-foot infravision. Speaks Utukku and can communicate telepathically with intelligent creatures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws and bite. Two claw attacks at 4d4 each and one bite at 3d4.
At will. Detect invisibility, read languages, know alignment, and detect magic.
Three times per day each. Teleport without error carrying up to 1,500 pounds, cause fear as a wand of fear, create darkness in a 30-foot radius, and produce a 12d6 lightning bolt.
Once per day each. Symbol of discord and control weather as an 18th-level mage.
Once per week each. Cause disease by touch and polymorph self into a human or humanoid form for a full day.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Only weapons with a magical bonus of +1 or higher can hit. 50% magic resistance. Lightning, fire, and poisonous gas deal half damage on a failed save or one-quarter on success. Add +4 to saves vs. poison. Immune to mental probes such as ESP and telepathy.

gm.title: Travel and Red Curse
lines: Once a century the utukku can plane shift from Carceri to the Prime Material Plane. After one year it returns automatically with up to 4,000 pounds of material. It neither gains Legacies nor requires cinnabryl.

gm.title: Description
lines: An undead ruler watches over its plunder and commands the warriors buried with it.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Perception 13, Stealth 12. Resists cold damage. Immune to necrotic and poison damage and to Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, and Poisoned. Darkvision 60 ft., truesight 30 ft. Languages known in life.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +5, Dex +2, Con +5, Int +0, Wis +1, Cha +5

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Aura of Authority. Allies within 10 ft. have advantage on attacks and saves while the buried lord is free of the Incapacitated condition.
Grave Goods Sense. Pinpoint anyone wearing or carrying its belongings or grave goods within 60 ft. and sense the direction of those objects within 1 mile.
Rejuvenation. After destruction, return at full HP in a new body 24 hours later, in a random unoccupied space within 100 ft. of the spot where it fell. Putting it to rest, usually by returning its remains to its burial mound, prevents this.
Sunlight Sensitivity. Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while in sunlight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Longsword attacks or two Longbow attacks.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) necrotic.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft. Hit 11 (2d8 + 2) piercing damage.
Corpse Breath (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 15-ft. cone make a DC 13 Constitution save. On failure, a creature is Poisoned for 1 minute and can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end it.
Disorienting Gaze. One creature the buried lord sees within 30 ft. makes a DC 13 Charisma save. On failure, it is Incapacitated and travels in a random direction whenever it moves. Repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. A success grants immunity to this buried lord’s gaze for 24 hours.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Uses Charisma, save DC 13, and requires no material components.
2/day: Bane.
1/day each: Enlarge/Reduce, Gaseous Form.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Mark Quarry (2/day). Mark one visible creature within 30 ft. until the start of the buried lord’s next turn. Its weapon hits against that creature deal an extra 1d6 of the weapon’s damage type.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Parry. Add 2 AC against one melee attack that would hit. The buried lord must see its attacker and wield a melee weapon or hold a shield.

A creature can remove a level by spending an action to drink a pint of water. Creatures immune to Exhaustion ignore the aura.
Infested Water. After every seven days it spends in an enclosed body of water up to 100 ft. in radius, it deposits eggs. They remain viable for 24 hours. A DC 15 Intelligence (Nature) check to inspect the water spots them. A Beast or Humanoid who drinks the water makes a DC 15 Constitution save or contracts a disease. Only one tadpole can mature per host. After each long rest, the host repeats the save. On failure, reduce its Strength score by 1d4. The reduction lasts until a long rest after the disease is cured. gm.title: Traits
lines: Shapechanger. If the vampire isn’t in sunlight or running water, it can use its action to polymorph into a Tiny bat or a Medium cloud of mist, or back into its true form. While in bat form, the vampire can’t speak, its walking speed is 5 feet, and it has a flying speed of 30 feet. Its statistics, other than its size and speed, are unchanged. Anything it is wearing transforms with it, but nothing it is carrying does. It reverts to its true form if it dies. While in mist form, the vampire can’t take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless, has a flying speed of 20 feet, can hover, and can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. In addition, if air can pass through a space, the mist can do so without squeezing, and it can’t pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws, and it is immune to all nonmagical damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight. Legendary Resistance (3/Day). If the vampire fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. Misty Escape. When it drops to 0 hit points outside its resting place, the vampire transforms into a cloud of mist (as in the Shapechanger trait) instead of falling unconscious, provided that it isn’t in sunlight or running water. If it can’t transform, it is destroyed. While it has 0 hit points in mist form, it can’t revert to its vampire form, and it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed. Once in its resting place, it reverts to its vampire form. It is then paralyzed until it regains at least 1 hit point. After spending 1 hour in its resting place with 0 hit points, it regains 1 hit point. Regeneration. The vampire regains 20 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point and isn’t in sunlight or running water. If the vampire takes radiant damage or damage from holy water, this trait doesn’t function at the start of the vampire’s next turn. Spider Climb. The vampire can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. Vampire Weaknesses. The vampire has the following flaws: Forbiddance. The vampire can’t enter a residence without an invitation from one of the occupants. Harmed by Running Water. The vampire takes 20 acid damage if it ends its turn in running water. Stake to the Heart. If a piercing weapon made of wood is driven into the vampire’s heart while the vampire is incapacitated in its resting place, the vampire is paralyzed until the stake is removed. Sunlight Hypersensitivity. The vampire takes 20 radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack (Vampire Form Only). The vampire makes two attacks, only one of which can be a bite attack. Unarmed Strike (Vampire Form Only). Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. Instead of dealing damage, the vampire can grapple the target (escape DC 18). Bite (Bat or Vampire Form Only). Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one willing creature, or a creature that is grappled by the vampire, incapacitated, or restrained. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. The target’s hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains hit points equal to that amount. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0. A humanoid slain in this way and then buried in the ground rises the following night as a vampire spawn under the vampire’s control. Charm. The vampire targets one humanoid it can see within 30 feet of it. If the target can see the vampire, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw against this magic or be charmed by the vampire. The charmed target regards the vampire as a trusted friend to be heeded and protected. Although the target isn’t under the vampire’s control, it takes the vampire’s requests or actions in the most favorable way it can, and it is a willing target for the vampire’s bite attack. Each time the vampire or the vampire’s companions do anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until the vampire is destroyed, is on a different plane of existence than the target, or takes a bonus action to end the effect. Children of the Night (1/Day). The vampire magically calls 2d4 swarms of bats or rats, provided that the sun isn’t up. While outdoors, the vampire can call 3d6 wolves instead. The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the vampire and obeying its spoken commands. The beasts remain for 1 hour, until the vampire dies, or until the vampire dismisses them as a bonus action.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The vampire can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The vampire regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Move. The vampire moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Unarmed Strike. The vampire makes one unarmed strike. Bite (Costs 2 Actions). The vampire makes one bite attack.

gm.title: Description
lines: A vampire drinks blood and must retreat to its coffin, crypt, or grave by day. It can carry its coffin or enough grave dirt elsewhere to establish another resting place.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Shapechanger. Outside sunlight and running water, the vampire can use an action to become a Tiny bat, a Medium cloud of mist, or its true form. As a bat, it cannot speak, has a walking speed of 5 ft. and flying speed of 30 ft., and otherwise retains its stats apart from size. Worn gear transforms with it, and carried gear does not. Death returns it to true form. As mist, it cannot use actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It weighs nothing, flies 20 ft. with hover, can stop in hostile creatures' spaces, fits anywhere air can pass without squeezing, and cannot pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves in mist form and is immune to nonmagical damage other than sunlight damage.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Misty Escape. At 0 HP outside its resting place, it becomes mist instead of falling Unconscious. It is destroyed if sunlight or running water prevents the change. At 0 HP in mist form, it cannot revert voluntarily and must reach its resting place in 2 hours or be destroyed. When it arrives, it reverts and is Paralyzed until it has at least 1 HP. An hour spent there at 0 HP restores 1 HP.
Regeneration. It regains 20 HP at the start of each turn if it has at least 1 HP and is outside sunlight and running water. Radiant damage or damage from holy water stops regeneration at the start of its next turn.
Spider Climb. It climbs difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
Undead Nature. It needs no air. A vampire without a formal burial rests beneath a foot of soil at the place where it became undead.

gm.title: Vampire weaknesses
lines:
Forbiddance. An occupant must invite the vampire before it enters a residence.
Harmed by Running Water. Ending a turn in running water deals 20 acid damage to it.
Stake to the Heart. If a wooden piercing weapon pierces its heart while it is Incapacitated at its resting place, it is Paralyzed until the weapon is removed.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. Starting its turn in sunlight deals 20 radiant damage to it. It has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks in sunlight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack (vampire form only). It makes two attacks, with at most one Bite.
Unarmed Strike (vampire form only). Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. It can instead Grapple the target on a hit (escape DC 18).
Bite (bat or vampire form only). Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature that is willing, Grappled by this vampire, Incapacitated, or Restrained. Hit 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. Reduce the target's maximum HP and heal the vampire by the necrotic damage taken. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a Long Rest, and the target dies if its maximum HP becomes 0. A humanoid killed this way and buried in the ground rises the next night as a Vampire Spawn under its control.
Charm. Choose one humanoid the vampire sees within 30 ft. If the target sees it, the target makes a DC 17 Wisdom save against magic. Failure leaves the target Charmed, treating the vampire as a trusted friend to protect and heed. The target interprets the vampire's actions and requests as favorably as it can and is willing to be bitten. It retains control of its own actions. Each harmful act by the vampire or its allies lets the target repeat the save, ending the effect on success. The charm ends after 24 hours, if the vampire is destroyed, if the two are on different planes, or if the vampire uses a Bonus Action to end it.
Children of the Night (1/day). If the sun is down, it magically calls 2d4 Swarms of Bats or Swarms of Rats. Outdoors it can call 3d6 Wolves instead. The creatures arrive after 1d4 rounds, ally with the vampire, and obey its spoken orders. They stay for 1 hour or until the vampire dies or dismisses them with a Bonus Action.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round, spent one option at a time after another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it can use them only after its first turn.
Move. It moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Unarmed Strike. It makes one Unarmed Strike.
Bite (2 actions). It makes one Bite attack.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines: Bats, rats, and wolves grow more numerous around its lair. Within 500 ft., plants wither and grow twisted and thorny, shadows stretch and sometimes move on their own, and fog clings to the ground and occasionally takes strange shapes. The effects end 2d6 days after the vampire is destroyed.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

Only one creature can be held this way. Moving while holding a Medium or smaller creature does not halve the vampire's speed.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +10, reach 5 ft., one creature Grappled by the vampire, Incapacitated, or Restrained. Hit 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. The target's maximum HP falls by the necrotic damage taken and the vampire heals that amount. Cure Ailment of 4th order or higher, Greater Restoration, or a similar supernatural effect can restore that maximum. A creature dies if this brings its maximum HP to 0. A humanoid killed this way rises at the following midnight as a vampire spawn under the vampire's control.

It flies up to twice its speed to an empty space, ignores difficult terrain and opportunity attacks, and can pass through creatures and objects. Each creature passed through makes a DC 18 Constitution save for 35 (10d6) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. The vampire then resumes its previous form.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:

On a failure it spends its reaction, if available, to move up to its speed to a location the vampire chooses. The vampire then chooses whether the victim falls Prone or makes a melee attack against a target the vampire picks. A creature that cannot be Charmed succeeds automatically. A creature with advantage against Charmed makes this save with advantage.

lines: Run, My Child. When an ally the vampire can see takes damage, that ally can move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks at the vampire's command.

Obey My Desire. Each creature within 60 ft. that hears the vampire makes a DC 18 Wisdom save or is Charmed until the end of this turn. Each creature Charmed this way immediately spends its reaction, if available, to make a melee attack against another creature, make one against itself, or fall Prone. The vampire picks the effect.
