The target interprets the vampire's actions and requests as favorably as it can and is willing to be bitten. It retains control of its own actions. Each harmful act by the vampire or its allies lets the target repeat the save, ending the effect on success. The charm ends after 24 hours, if the vampire is destroyed, if the two are on different planes, or if the vampire uses a Bonus Action to end it.
Children of the Night (1/day). If the sun is down, it magically calls 2d4 Swarms of Bats or Swarms of Rats. Outdoors it can call 3d6 Wolves instead. The creatures arrive after 1d4 rounds, ally with the vampire, and obey its spoken orders. They stay for 1 hour or until the vampire dies or dismisses them with a Bonus Action.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round, spent one option at a time after another creature's turn. It regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it can use them only after its first turn.
Move. It moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Unarmed Strike. It makes one Unarmed Strike.
Bite (2 actions). It makes one Bite attack.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines: Bats, rats, and wolves grow more numerous around its lair. Within 500 ft., plants wither and grow twisted and thorny, shadows stretch and sometimes move on their own, and fog clings to the ground and occasionally takes strange shapes. The effects end 2d6 days after the vampire is destroyed.

gm.title: Description
lines: A vampire that barters with powers of darkness for forbidden magic. Choose a concealed resting place when you prepare its lair.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Small or Medium undead, lawful evil

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day, or 4/day in its lair). After failing a save, the vampire can spend one use to succeed.
Shadow Escape. If the vampire reaches 0 HP away from its resting place, it teleports there. If it can’t teleport, it is destroyed. It can’t teleport this way in sunlight or running water. After teleporting, it is Paralyzed for 1 hour, then recovers 1 HP.
Vampire Weakness. It needs an occupant’s invitation to enter a residence. It takes 20 Acid damage if it ends its turn in running water. If someone drives a weapon that deals Piercing damage into its heart while it is Incapacitated in its resting place, it remains Paralyzed until the weapon comes out. At the start of its turn in sunlight, it takes 20 Radiant damage. Sunlight gives it Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using any combination of Grave Strike and Sickening Ray.
Grave Strike. Melee attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 9 (1d8 + 5) Slashing damage and 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage.
Sickening Ray. Ranged attack, +10 to hit, range 120 ft. A hit deals 16 (2d10 + 5) Necrotic damage and leaves the target Poisoned until the start of the vampire’s next turn.
Hunger of Hadar (Recharge 5–6). Cast Hunger of Hadar at level 5 without components, using Charisma with spell save DC 18.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Sanguine Drain. Choose a creature the vampire can see within 30 ft. that is neither a Construct nor an Undead. On a failed DC 18 Constitution save, it takes 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage. Reduce its HP maximum by the damage it actually took and restore that many HP to the vampire.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses, or 4 in its lair. Spend one immediately after another creature’s turn to select one option. The vampire recovers spent uses at the start of its turn and cannot use them while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Beguile. Cast Command without components, using Charisma with spell save DC 18. Beguile then becomes unavailable until the vampire’s next turn starts.
Umbral Strike. Move up to half its Speed and make one Grave Strike or Sickening Ray attack.

gm.title: In its lair
lines: 15,000 XP. Legendary Resistance increases to 4/day and Legendary Actions increase to 4 uses.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Children of the Night. From dusk to dawn, Beasts of Medium size or smaller are Charmed while within 1 mile of the lair.
Looming Shadows. Shadows appear to move on their own. A creature that finishes a Short Rest within 1 mile must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save to benefit from that rest. The vampire and its allies are exempt.
Mists. Persistent fog makes the area within 1 mile Lightly Obscured. The vampire and creatures it chooses ignore the fog.
All three effects end as soon as the vampire dies or moves its lair.

lines: Necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

gm.title: Traits

Regeneration. The fungus regains 3 hit points at the start of its turn. Cold, fire, or necrotic damage prevents this recovery at the start of its next turn. It dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and this trait fails to restore any.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.

gm.title: Russet Mold
lines:
Identification. This reddish-brown mold grows in darkness and damp warmth. On metal, a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Nature) or Wisdom (Survival) check distinguishes it from rust.
Exposure. A creature that comes within 5 ft. must make a DC 13 Constitution save against the released spores. On a failure, it is poisoned and takes 7 (2d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns as mold sprouts on it. At the end of each of its turns, it can repeat the save to end the effect. Magic that neutralizes poison or cures disease also destroys the infestation.
New growth. A creature dies if this damage reduces it to 0 HP. If the victim is a beast, giant, or humanoid, its corpse produces newborn Vegepygmies after 24 hours. A Small corpse produces one, Medium two, Large four, Huge eight, and Gargantuan sixteen. Moldies born from beasts take the form of Thornies.
Clearing it. Each point of acid, necrotic, or radiant damage clears 1 square foot. A pound of salt, a gallon of alcohol, or magic that cures disease clears a 10-foot square. Sunlight destroys exposed patches. Weapons and most other damage have no effect.

gm.title: Description
lines: An older vegepygmy grows tougher and develops spore clusters. Other vegepygmies defer to it as their chief.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Plant Camouflage. The vegepygmy has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in terrain where vegetation provides ample concealment.
Regeneration. The vegepygmy regains 5 HP at the start of its turn. Cold, fire, or necrotic damage suppresses this trait at the start of its next turn. The vegepygmy dies only if it starts its turn at 0 HP and fails to regenerate.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make either two Claws attacks or two melee Spear attacks.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage if wielded in two hands for a melee attack.
Spores (1/day). A cloud extends 15 ft. from the chief and spreads around corners. Each creature in the area other than a Plant must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or be poisoned. While poisoned this way, the target takes 9 (2d8) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

gm.title: Spore infection mechanics
lines: If a creature dies while infected by the chief’s spores, its corpse produces vegepygmies under the Russet Mold rules. A Humanoid or Giant corpse produces one or more vegepygmies after one day. A Beast corpse can produce a Thorny Vegepygmy instead.

gm.title: Description
lines: Victor Mordenheim is the Lamordian surgeon who built Adam. He works in Schloss Mordenheim, where his machines keep his injured wife Elise von Brandthofen alive.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A lean, pale man who looks to be in his thirties, with prematurely grey hair, tired blue eyes and a faint scar on his forehead. He wears plain brown wool or a surgical gown.

gm.title: What brought him here
lines: Victor raised Adam as a son and tried to teach him to live among people. Adam attacked Elise von Brandthofen, vanished with Eva, and left Victor to save what remained of his wife.

gm.title: What he wants
lines: Victor wants a new body for Elise von Brandthofen. He will rob graves and comb hospices for suitable remains. Locals blame him for disappearances that Adam causes.

gm.title: Running Victor
lines: He rarely starts a fight and has no weapon training. He can make one attack with whatever weapon he has. Its damage depends on the weapon.

gm.title: Shared curse
lines: Victor cannot die while Adam lives. He shares Adam’s hit point total and can regrow from a surviving piece of his body.
Adam feels pain inflicted on Victor. If Victor’s body is completely destroyed, his spirit seeks a recently dead human man. The body takes on Victor’s appearance within a week.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Exploit Opening (3/day). Gain advantage on an attack roll.
Mind Link. The bosses of the Amethyst Knife can speak telepathically with one another across any distance on the same plane.
Kinetic Buildup. Each melee weapon hit adds 5 ft. to her speed and grants one additional reaction until the start of her next turn. The bonuses stack.
Psionic Wound (3/day). When Mindrazor hits, she can force a DC 17 Intelligence save. On a failure, the target is vulnerable to psychic damage for 1 minute. Repeat the save at the end of each turn to end it. No action required.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Shared Condition. When the creature becomes Blinded, Charmed, Dazed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned, it can transfer the condition and its remaining duration to a willing Amethyst Knife boss within 60 ft. who neither has the condition nor is immune to it. The condition ends for the original creature. This reaction works even while Incapacitated.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Amethyst Knife. The party can use one villain party action per round, after an enemy's turn. Each action is available once per encounter, in any order. The member taking it must be present and able to act.
Action 4, Telepathic Tirade. Pick one visible creature within 30 ft. Until the end of its next turn, it rolls ability checks, attacks, and saves with disadvantage and takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage each time one fails.

gm.title: Recoverable Magic Item
lines: Mindrazor. Very rare +1 rapier, attunement required. It holds 3 charges and refills at dawn. On a hit spend 1 charge to force a DC 17 Intelligence save. A failure gives the target vulnerability to psychic damage for 1 minute. The target can try the save again at the end of each turn.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: While Dazed, a creature can use only one of its movement, action, or bonus action on its turn. Gaining Dazed ends the turn if it happens during that turn. Extra actions such as Haste or Action Surge still work. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can end the condition.

lines: Perception 15, Stealth 18. Resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks and the Charmed and Unconscious conditions. No special senses in the statistics line. Languages Common, Sylvan.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +1, Dex +5, Con +1, Int +0, Wis +2, Cha +6

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fey Resilience. It resists Charmed and Unconscious.
Forest’s Defender. Nonmagical vegetation, including thorns and spines, does not slow or damage it. It has advantage on initiative in forested terrain.
Forest Sight. It sees clearly through light obscurity and treats dim light as bright.
Heightened Hearing and Sight. Perception 20 when using hearing or sight.
Poisoned Weapons. Each weapon hit deals an extra 3d6 poison damage, already listed below.
Speak with Beasts. It can speak with Beasts as if they shared a language.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks using Shortsword or Shortbow.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing plus 10 (3d6) poison damage.
Denizens of the Wilds (1/day). Call 1d4 wolves, one brown bear, or one flinderbeast. They arrive in 1d4 rounds, act as allies, and obey spoken commands. They stay for up to one hour, until the vila dies, or until it dismisses them as a bonus action.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Song of the Forest. Choose up to two visible creatures within 30 ft. Each target that hears the song makes a DC 14 Wisdom save. On failure, Ancient Lullaby makes the target Unconscious for 1 minute, ending if it takes damage or if another creature spends an action waking it. Fascinating Melody makes it Stunned until the end of its next turn. Luckless Tune imposes disadvantage on attacks and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

lines:

gm.title: Description
lines: An enormous fungal creature that seizes prey and grafts it to its own body.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Rotting Slam attacks.
Rotting Slam. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.
Spore Bomb (Recharge 5–6). Center a 20-ft.-radius Sphere on a point the necrohulk can see within 60 ft. Each creature in the Sphere makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 28 (8d6) Necrotic damage and is Poisoned until the start of the necrohulk's next turn. It cannot regain Hit Points while Poisoned in this way. On a success, it takes half damage only.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Absorb Body. Choose one Small or Medium creature the necrohulk can see within 5 ft. The target makes a DC 15 Strength save. On a failure, the necrohulk pulls the target into its space and grafts it to its body. It can have only one target grafted at a time. The grafted target is Restrained, has Disadvantage on Constitution saves, and moves with the necrohulk. If the grafted target dies, its body is destroyed and the necrohulk regains 10 Hit Points. The target or a creature within 5 ft. of the necrohulk can use an action to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check. On a success, the target is freed and moves to an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the necrohulk.

gm.title: Description
lines: The printed encounter presents an expert traveling with a caravan. He may try to drive attackers away with the evil eye.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Dagger +0 melee for 1d4, or light crossbow +0 ranged for 1d8.
Evil Eye (Ex). Standard-action gaze against one target; merely looking at the expert does not trigger it. The printed male example’s Will DC is 11. Select one of the following on a failed save:
Paralysis. Paralyzed for 1d4 + 1 rounds. If failure exceeds four, instead paralyzed for 2 rounds, then convulsions deal 1d8 each round for 3 rounds. Afterward DC 15 Fortitude or die; on success the victim is unconscious but easily awakened.
Fear. Fear spell effect for 1d4 + 1 rounds.
Domination. Dominate person effect for 1d4 + 1 rounds.
Suggestion. Suggestion spell effect for one day or until the task is complete.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Initiative +0, touch AC 10, flat-footed 13, studded leather +3. BAB/grapple +0/+0, space/reach 5 ft./5 ft., Fort +0, Ref +0, Will +4. Speaks Patterna; many know domain languages. The source gives Evil Eye DC 10 + half HD + Cha for a male and 12 + half HD + Cha for a female encounter NPC.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +5, Diplomacy +5, Listen +6, Sense Motive +8, Spot +6, Survival +8, and four ranks in a Craft, Perform or Profession skill. Voice of Wrath and Skill Focus in the selected skill. The printed racial +2 on Sense Motive and Survival is represented in the sample values.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land. Gang of 3–6 or a caravan of 20–40 plus 30% noncombatants, four 3rd-level guards, a 5th-level captain, and a 7th-level raunie. Usually neutral, standard treasure. Guards may try to capture enemies instead of killing them.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The entry does not give a specific range for Evil Eye. Use the standard 3.5 gaze range as a table default if needed.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Plate. Saving throws Str +11, Con +8, Cha +10. Skills Acrobatics +3, Athletics +11, Deception +10, Intimidation +10. Resists acid and necrotic damage. Blindsight 30 ft., darkvision 120 ft. Passive Perception 11. Common and Draconic.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Exploit Opening (3/day). The creature can gain advantage on an attack roll it makes.
Reckless. At the start of her turn, Vivienn can gain advantage on all melee weapon attacks she makes that turn. If she does, attacks against her have advantage until the start of her next turn.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Godslayer Axe attacks.
Godslayer Axe. Melee weapon attack +11, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 14 (1d12 + 8) slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) necrotic damage. A Celestial takes an extra 18 (4d8) necrotic damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions

lines: Powers are supernatural and have no components. Antimagic Field, Counterspell, and Dispel Magic affect spells or magic and do not stop powers. A creature with a melee power attack can use it for an opportunity attack.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

lines: A pitch-black scavver about twenty feet long with one large eye and a sharklike maw. It hunts alone and can send an invisible ray of fear from its eye.

lines: Unusual Nature. The scavver can live without air.

lines:

While swallowed, the creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover from attacks and other effects outside the scavver, and takes 11 (2d10) acid damage at the start of each of the scavver’s turns.
If a creature inside the scavver deals at least 25 damage to it in one turn, the scavver makes a DC 20 Constitution save at that turn’s end. On a failure, it ejects the swallowed creature, which falls prone within 10 ft. of the scavver. If the scavver dies, the swallowed creature stops being restrained and can spend 10 ft. of movement to crawl out, emerging prone.

gm.title: Description
lines: A vampire’s chosen companion survives an interrupted Dark Kiss. The vorlog charms a replacement and drains their Wisdom to keep them devoted.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC components +2 Dex, +3 natural, +4 chain shirt. Touch AC 12, flat-footed AC 17. Base attack +6, grapple +10. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +7, Ref +4, Will +3.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack and full attack as printed. Unarmed strike +10/+5 melee (1d3 + 4 nonlethal and Wisdom Drain), short sword +10/+5 melee (1d6 + 4, 19–20/×2), or masterwork mighty longbow +9 ranged (1d8 + 4, 19–20/×2).
Animal Rage (Su). At will, animals within 50 ft. make a DC 14 Will save or rage as the spell at caster level 12 and attack the nearest creature, even the vorlog.
Charm Person (Sp). At will at caster level 6, Will DC 12.
Wisdom Drain (Su). The unarmed hit deals 1d3 Wisdom damage to a living target. At Wisdom below 3 it becomes a lost one under the vorlog’s control. The vorlog keeps its surrogate at or below half their normal Wisdom.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 5/silver and magic. Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, sleep, and paralysis. Fast Healing (Ex) restores 1 HP per hour while at 1 HP or more, or 1 HP per round if the surrogate is physically present. At 0 HP or less it becomes a puddle of tears, moves at speed 20 ft., can climb walls and pass through tiny cracks, and must reach a dark haven in 1d4 hours or evaporate. After resting 8 hours it resumes humanoid form. Direct sunlight deals 1d6 damage each round. It will not approach a good deity’s holy symbol presented with conviction. It needs food and Wisdom and dies after three months without a surrogate.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Climb +16, Craft (bowmaking) +4, Diplomacy +3, Listen +4, Move Silently +13, Ride +4, Spot +4. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Dodge, Improved Critical (short sword), Improved Initiative, Improved Unarmed Strike, Point Blank Shot, Power Attack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any land and underground. Solitary. Usually chaotic, always evil. Standard treasure. Gear includes 50 +1 arrows and a ring of climbing. It retains its former languages. A charmed victim who drinks the vorlog’s blood for three consecutive nights becomes its surrogate.

gm.title: Template for another encounter
lines: Apply to a humanoid or monstrous humanoid. Keep type, size, speed, attacks, damage, saves, and existing special abilities. Increase Hit Dice one die size to a maximum of d12. Add +3 natural armor, +4 Str, +2 Dex, +2 Cha, and a +8 racial bonus to Move Silently. Add Alertness and Improved Unarmed Strike if missing. Add the vorlog attacks, traits and weaknesses above. Animal Rage Will DC is 10 + half the vorlog’s HD + Cha modifier. Charm Person Will DC is 11 + Cha modifier. CR is base +1, level adjustment base +8, and advancement by class.

gm.title: Description
lines: This fledgling was a human warrior. It puts victims into a fever sleep and can flee as a swarm.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Fledgling sample, 5th-level human warrior. Initiative +9. AC components +5 Dex, +5 natural, +1 deflection. Touch 16, flat-footed 16. Base attack +5, grapple +11. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +4.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +11 melee for 1d4 + 6 and filth fever.
Full attack. Two of the listed claws.
Fever Sleep (Su). Standard action against one target within 30 ft. who meets its eyes. Will DC 12 or sleep as the spell at caster level 12 without a Hit Dice limit. Feeding does not awaken the target.
Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living creature in a grapple. Each round the pin is maintained, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP. A victim must also save against filth fever.
Filth fever (Ex). Any living victim damaged by a claw or blood drain makes a DC 12 Fortitude save. Incubation is 1d3 days. The disease deals 1d3 Dexterity and 1d3 Constitution damage.
Children of the Night (Su). Once per day as a standard action, call 6d10 HD of monstrous vermin. They arrive after 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 5/iron and magic in the sample’s stat line. Cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +3, spider climb, and undead traits.
Disease (Ex). The strain carries one permanent disease. It also picks up injury- or contact-transmitted diseases when it feeds on an infected victim. Add its Cha modifier to the disease DC. Each secondary disease’s DC falls by 1 each day after acquisition. At DC 0 it loses that disease. A DC 15 Heal check identifies diseases it carries.
Alternate Form (Su). As a standard action, use polymorph at caster level 12 to change into a dire rat, a rat swarm, or a swarm of Fine vermin until changing again or until sunrise. A swarm has as many 1-HP members as the vampire has total HP. Each member killed costs the vampire 1 HP. The swarm members still carry its diseases.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid killed by its disease rises as vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. A victim drained to Constitution 0 returns as spawn if it had 4 or fewer HD or as a vrykolaka if it had 5 or more. A creator controls its spawn until it dies.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines:
Garlic, anise, a continuous line of aniseed, and a strongly brandished holy symbol keep it away. It cannot enter an immaculate room or cross running water unaided. Still or stagnant water does not trouble it.
Direct sunlight leaves it with a single move or attack action. It is destroyed in the next round if it cannot escape the light. Immersion in running water takes away one-third of its HP each round and destroys it at the end of round 3. A vampire strain whose base creature has a swim speed retains it and escapes the immersion weakness.
At 1 HP or more it heals 5 HP per round. At 0 HP or less it flees as a swarm. At least half the swarm must get to its coffin within 2 hours or it is destroyed. After 1 hour there it reaches 1 HP and resumes healing.
An iron spike through its skull kills it while the spike remains. Burn the body completely to keep it from returning. A casting of remove disease forces a Fortitude save or bestows two negative levels. While it sleeps in its coffin or is incapacitated it automatically fails this save. It is destroyed permanently at negative levels equal to or greater than its HD. When destroyed, it dissolves into vapors like stinking cloud at caster level 12.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +8, Handle Animal +4, Hide +13, Intimidate +6, Jump +12, Listen +13, Move Silently +13, Search +6, Sense Motive +11, Spot +13. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack, Run.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any environment in Ravenloft. Solitary, pair, or gang of 2–5. An organized group can contain 1–2 full vampires and 2–5 vampire spawn. Speaks languages known in life. Always evil. Standard treasure. The printed warrior wears a ring of protection +1.

gm.title: Template and age
lines: Apply the strain to a humanoid or monstrous humanoid using the 3.5 vampire template as the base. Keep its size, base attack, saves, skill points, d12 HD and applicable original powers. Constitution is absent. These age entries give the changes to Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha, speed, natural AC and Outcast Rating (OR) against non-vrykolakas. Intelligence has a minimum of 3. Every age tier requires cold iron and magic to bypass damage reduction. Apply one age row only. The sample already incorporates its age. For unlisted save DCs use 10 + half HD, rounded down, + Cha modifier. Filth fever uses 12 + Cha modifier instead. Claw damage follows the size table if the base creature has no claw attack. Where the printed example differs, use its own attack line.

gm.title: Age modifiers
lines:
Fledgling. Abilities +6/+8/−6/+4/+2. Speed +0 ft., DR 5, fast healing 5, turn resistance +3, natural AC +5, OR +2, CR +1.
Mature. Abilities +6/+10/−4/+4/+2. Speed +0 ft., DR 10, fast healing 5, turn resistance +3, natural AC +5, OR +2, CR +1.
Old. Abilities +8/+10/−4/+6/+4. Speed +10 ft., DR 10, fast healing 6, turn resistance +4, natural AC +6, OR +3, CR +2.
Ancient. Abilities +8/+12/−2/+6/+4. Speed +10 ft., DR 15, fast healing 6, turn resistance +5, natural AC +6, OR +4, CR +2.
Eminent. Abilities +10/+12/−2/+8/+6. Speed +20 ft., DR 15, fast healing 8, turn resistance +6, natural AC +7, OR +5, CR +3.
Patriarch. Abilities +12/+14/+0/+10/+8. Speed +30 ft., DR 20, fast healing 10, turn resistance +7, natural AC +7, OR +6, CR +4.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The sample says DR 5/iron and magic. The age table specifies cold iron and magic. The sample’s claw die is 1d4 even though the strain table gives 1d6 as the default for Medium creatures. For template use, the p. 204 spawn paragraph says “vampire” before referring to the new vrykolaka.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Arcane anomalies (Drakkenheim)
lines:
Printed source. Appendix D, p. 225. Roll 1d20 for the anomaly.
1. Gravity fails in a 100-ft. radius for 1 hour. Unattended objects drift. Creatures float and can move as if climbing by pushing or pulling against surfaces or fixed objects.
2. The nearest creature is subject to Hideous Laughter, save DC 15. It babbles instead of laughing.
3. Creatures within 60 ft. are Stunned for 1 round, with no save.
4. The nearest creature gains Blink for 1 minute and slips through time when it vanishes.
5. In a 20-ft. radius, creatures make a DC 15 Constitution save. Failure deals 8d6 radiant damage and Blinds for 1 round. Wood turns into glass.
6. For 1 minute, attacks that hit within 60 ft. show a vision of the target dying from the hit.
7. Creatures within 30 ft. are subject to Irresistible Dance, save DC 15.
8. Part of the surroundings becomes a delerium elemental appropriate to its element.
9. The GM chooses or randomly determines an extraplanar creature. It stays for 1 hour and is friendly to whoever triggered the anomaly.
10. Humanoid corpses within 120 ft. rise as hostile Haze Husks.
11. The shadows of 1d6 random creatures come alive and attack their owners. Destroying a shadow leaves its owner without one for 24 hours.
12. Creatures within 60 ft. become Invisible for 1 minute, ending for each creature when it attacks or casts a spell.
13. The nearest creature makes a DC 15 Constitution save against 8d8 necrotic damage, halved on success. The next three nearest creatures within 60 ft. each heal the damage it took.
14. Hypnotic Pattern appears, save DC 15. Those Incapacitated by it weep.
15. Black Tentacles appears in the area for 1 hour, escape DC 15.
16. Objects within 60 ft. animate for 1 hour as under Animate Objects. They speak and remain nonhostile.
17. The nearest creature becomes an awakened shrub for 1 hour or until it drops to 0 HP, with no save.
18. Up to six random creatures within 120 ft. are subject to Slow for 1 minute, save DC 15.
19. One random creature within 60 ft. gains Haste for 1 minute.
20. A bowl of flowers and an aquatic mammal appear 100 ft. overhead.

gm.title: Description
lines: A Wallaran totem animal visits the deepest dreams to offer advice. It sometimes leaves a token the dreamer finds upon waking.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: All three totems are solitary, very rare, and neutral or good, usually lawful. Intelligence 19–20. Special morale. No treasure, Legacies or cinnabryl requirement.

gm.title: Actions
lines: A spirit can cast at will as an 18th-level mage, with no casting time or components. It prefers to turn attackers into harmless creatures with polymorph other. It can disappear when attacked or replace the dreamer’s weapons with harmless objects. It speaks directly to the dreaming mind.

gm.title: Kangaroo
lines: Medium. Movement 18. Three attacks for 1d3, 1d3 and 2d4. Its followers are known for acting quickly by Wallaran standards.

gm.title: Koala
lines: Small. Movement 6. One attack for 1d2. Its followers often provide food for the community.

gm.title: Kookaburra
lines: Tiny. Movement 6 and fly 18, maneuverability A. One attack for 1 damage. Nocturnal. Its followers often guide interactions with outsiders or care for children.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: Clashes occur only in the Dreamworld. Only magical weapons physically brought there can hit the spirit. A weapon that appears merely because its owner is dreaming has no effect. All three totems have 95% magic resistance.

gm.title: Experience
lines: Award 1,000 XP for a peaceful encounter with the spirit. There is no XP for fighting it.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The Kookaburra size figure in the table appears as 18 feet. Its description gives 18 inches and the table classifies it as Tiny.

lines:

Possession (recharge 6). One visible humanoid within 5 ft. makes a DC 13 Charisma save. On failure the witch vanishes and controls the target’s body. The target stays aware, is Incapacitated, and cannot control its body. The witch keeps its own alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and Charmed and Frightened immunities. It otherwise uses the target’s statistics without its knowledge, proficiencies, or class features. Only effects that turn Undead can target it during possession. The effect also ends if the body falls to 0 HP, the witch ends it as a bonus action, or it is turned or expelled by a spell such as Dispel Evil and Good. On ending, the witch appears in a vacant space within 5 ft. A humanoid that succeeds or is freed is immune to this witch’s Possession for 24 hours.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Mutate Host. While possessing a creature, force it to make a DC 13 Charisma save. On failure it gains one contamination level and automatically acquires a random mutation in place of the normal mutation check.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Description
lines: Wastriliths stake out bodies of water tainted by the Abyss. They can foul water on land and in containers as well as underwater.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The wastrilith breathes air and water.
Corrupt Water. At the start of the wastrilith’s turn, exposed water within 30 ft. becomes corrupted. Underwater, the affected area is lightly obscured until a current flushes it out. Water held in a container stays corrupted until it evaporates.
A creature that drinks or swims in the water makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a success, it is immune to the foul water for 24 hours. On a failure, it takes 14 (4d6) poison damage and is poisoned for 1 minute. At the end of the minute, it repeats the save. On a failure, it takes 18 (4d8) poison damage and remains poisoned until it finishes a long rest.
Another demon that uses an action to drink the water gains 11 (2d10) temporary hit points.
Magic Resistance. The wastrilith has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claws attacks, and use Grasping Spout.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 30 (4d12 + 4) piercing damage.
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (4d6 + 4) slashing damage.
Grasping Spout. The wastrilith magically hurls a jet of water at one creature it can see within 60 ft. It makes a DC 17 Strength save, with disadvantage if underwater. On a failure, it takes 22 (4d8 + 4) acid damage and is pulled up to 60 ft. toward the wastrilith. On a success, it takes half the damage and stays in place.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Undertow. If the wastrilith is underwater, water within 60 ft. becomes difficult terrain for all other creatures until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Optional Abyssal corruption mechanics
lines: Use the 2014 Dungeon Master’s Guide’s optional Abyssal Corruption rule if you want the poisoned creature to risk corruption after drinking the foul water.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC +2 Dex, +6 natural. Touch AC 12, flat-footed AC 16. Base attack +6, grapple +10. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +6, Ref +4, Will +4.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +10 melee for 2d6 + 4 plus the listed energy drain. Full attack makes two such slams or uses a weapon at +10 melee for weapon damage +4.
Memory Drain (Su). A hit on its living counterpart calls for a DC 15 Will save. On failure, the victim takes one negative level in place of physical damage, and the golem gains the memories and abilities of the victim’s newest remaining level. If the victim escapes while partly drained, they make a DC 16 Madness save each week until the golem is destroyed. A completely drained victim is comatose and alive. If the drained counterpart later dies, the golem melts.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Damage reduction 10/magic. Immune to cold and electrical attacks. The stat block lists regeneration and vulnerability to fire.
Magic Immunity (Ex). The golem has the usual dread golem immunities. Magical fire melts its features, revealing the disguise.
Construct traits. Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, disease and similar effects. Critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, energy drain and death from massive damage do not affect it, subject to the exceptions below.

gm.title: Dread golem commands
lines: The creator can give commands from within 60 ft. if the golem can see and hear them. It follows the last command and responds to attacks against it. Some dread golems act independently.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Climb +7, Hide +6, Jump +7, Listen +4, Move Silently +5, Spot +3, Survival +3, Swim +7. Improved Initiative, Power Attack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any terrain. Solitary, always chaotic evil, no treasure. Advances to 9–12 HD (Large) or 13–16 HD (Huge).

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The save line prints “Wis +4” after Fortitude and Reflex. Read it as Will +4. The source gives no spell list or regeneration rate. Its only described energy-drain procedure is Memory Drain against the living counterpart.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A willow with hanging branches that shed salty tears.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Resists bludgeoning and piercing. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12. Speaks Common, Elvish, and Sylvan.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
False Appearance. A motionless willow looks like an ordinary tree.
Flammable. Fire damage ignites it for 1 minute. It takes 7 (2d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns while burning. Cold damage puts it out, or a creature can spend an action to extinguish it.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Frenzied Branch attacks.
Frenzied Branch. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, 30-ft. reach, one target. On a hit, deal 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning, plus 3 (1d6) fire if the willow is burning.
Tugging Roots. Choose a visible point on the ground within 60 ft. Each creature in a 10-ft. sphere centered there makes a DC 14 Strength save. On a failure, it falls Prone and the roots pull it up to 30 ft. toward the willow. It takes 4 (1d8) bludgeoning for every 10 ft. moved.
Willow’s Tears. Each creature within 15 ft. makes a DC 14 Wisdom save or becomes Charmed by the willow. Affected creatures cannot willingly move farther than 15 ft. from it and repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. Taking damage ends the charm on that creature.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Tree Transformation. When a creature within 5 ft. deals slashing damage to the willow, that creature makes a DC 14 Constitution save. If it fails, its feet take root and it is Restrained. It repeats the save at the end of its next turn. A success frees it. A failure makes it Petrified as a tree of its own size, with its face visible in the trunk. If the willow dies, the petrified creature returns to its original form. The Cure Ailment power or Lesser Restoration spell also ends the effect.

gm.title: Encounter uses
lines: Place the willow beside a path where its branches can reach across the road. Pull targets into range of its tears and track which creatures have a Tree Transformation save due on their next turn.

gm.title: Lycanthrope encounter rules
lines:
Printed source. Lycanthrope, pp. 137 and 148.
Alternate Form (Su). Where available, take or leave an animal or hybrid form as a standard action. Equipment does not change. Entering either form heals as a day of rest. A slain lycanthrope returns to humanoid form where it has one, but severed parts keep their animal shape. An afflicted creature normally gains one alternate form and can struggle to control it.
Curse of Lycanthropy (Su). A qualifying bite to a humanoid within one size category requires Fortitude DC 18 or transmits the curse. Bludgeoning or nonpenetrating attacks cannot transmit it. Afflicted lycanthropes can spread it in Ravenloft. The general text specifies animal form, but a listed hybrid curse also uses this procedure at the table. Use any strain-specific exception below.
Natural lycanthropes generally have DR 10/silver in animal or hybrid form, while afflicted ones have DR 5/silver. Some strains name a different material. Low-light vision and scent work in any form unless the profile specifies otherwise. Lycanthropic empathy allows simple communication, gives a +4 racial bonus on attitude checks with the corresponding normal or dire animal, and permits simple commands to friendly animals.
A spellcaster cannot use verbal, somatic, or material components in animal form and cannot use verbal components in hybrid form. Apply the printed encounter stats for each form.

gm.title: Player lycanthropy
lines:
A character keeps its own statistics except for the changes listed here. It gains the printed nonhumanoid speeds, damage immunities, traits, and actions that require no equipment, plus proficiency with the lycanthrope's natural attacks. Use the listed natural weapon damage. The character cannot speak in animal form.
Only a humanoid that is not already a lycanthrope saves against the curse when hit by a curse-bearing attack. The Constitution save DC is 8 + the attacking lycanthrope's proficiency bonus + its Constitution modifier. A character who resists the curse keeps their usual alignment and personality in humanoid form. The full moon forces them into animal or hybrid form until it wanes. A character who embraces the curse acquires the lycanthrope's alignment and can eventually learn to shift at will. The DM can take control of the character until the curse is removed. Remove Curse can end an acquired curse. A natural-born lycanthrope needs Wish.
Raise Strength to 19 if lower. Bear and hybrid forms gain +1 AC from natural armor. Use Strength for natural weapon attack and damage rolls.

gm.title: Nonhuman lycanthropes
lines: The printed blocks assume a human. For a lycanthrope of another ancestry, the DM can retain one or more traits from its humanoid form, such as Fey Ancestry for an elf.

lines: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 206–207 and 208. The player sidebar erratum clarifies curse eligibility. The profiles apply that limit to the curse-bearing attacks. Immunity wording follows the global errata.

gm.title: Lycanthrope encounter rules
lines:
Printed source. Lycanthrope, pp. 137 and 148.
Alternate Form (Su). Where available, take or leave an animal or hybrid form as a standard action. Equipment does not change. Entering either form heals as a day of rest. A slain lycanthrope returns to humanoid form where it has one, but severed parts keep their animal shape. An afflicted creature normally gains one alternate form and can struggle to control it.
Curse of Lycanthropy (Su). A qualifying bite to a humanoid within one size category requires Fortitude DC 18 or transmits the curse. Bludgeoning or nonpenetrating attacks cannot transmit it. Afflicted lycanthropes can spread it in Ravenloft. The general text specifies animal form, but a listed hybrid curse also uses this procedure at the table. Use any strain-specific exception below.
Natural lycanthropes generally have DR 10/silver in animal or hybrid form, while afflicted ones have DR 5/silver. Some strains name a different material. Low-light vision and scent work in any form unless the profile specifies otherwise. Lycanthropic empathy allows simple communication, gives a +4 racial bonus on attitude checks with the corresponding normal or dire animal, and permits simple commands to friendly animals.
A spellcaster cannot use verbal, somatic, or material components in animal form and cannot use verbal components in hybrid form. Apply the printed encounter stats for each form.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Warm forest of the Verdurous Lands. Solitary, group of 5–8, or pride of 5–20 with one 6-HD leader. Standard treasure. Usually lawful neutral.

gm.title: Actions
lines:

When the pack stalks someone in the jungle, the target can make a Spot check to notice the ambush. An unaware target is flat-footed when the pack attacks.

gm.title: Player lycanthropy
lines:
A character keeps its own statistics except for the changes listed here. It gains the printed nonhumanoid speeds, damage immunities, traits, and actions that require no equipment, plus proficiency with the lycanthrope's natural attacks. Use the listed natural weapon damage. The character cannot speak in animal form.
Only a humanoid that is not already a lycanthrope saves against the curse when hit by a curse-bearing attack. The Constitution save DC is 8 + the attacking lycanthrope's proficiency bonus + its Constitution modifier. A character who resists the curse keeps their usual alignment and personality in humanoid form. The full moon forces them into animal or hybrid form until it wanes. A character who embraces the curse acquires the lycanthrope's alignment and can eventually learn to shift at will. The DM can take control of the character until the curse is removed. Remove Curse can end an acquired curse. A natural-born lycanthrope needs Wish.
Raise Dexterity to 15 if lower. Use the higher of Strength or Dexterity for Bite attack and damage rolls.

gm.title: Nonhuman lycanthropes
lines: The printed blocks assume a human. For a lycanthrope of another ancestry, the DM can retain one or more traits from its humanoid form, such as Fey Ancestry for an elf.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 206–207 and 209. The player sidebar erratum clarifies curse eligibility. The profiles apply that limit to the curse-bearing attacks. Immunity wording follows the global errata.

On a failure, it is cursed. If a cursed target drops to 0 HP, it becomes a Wererat with 10 HP under the DM's control instead. On a success, the target is immune to this wererat's curse for 24 hours.

Hand Crossbow (Humanoid or hybrid form only). Ranged attack, +5 to hit, range 30/120 ft. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

lines: Shape-Shift. Take the shape of a Medium rat-humanoid hybrid or a Small rat, or return to its true Humanoid form. Game statistics are shared across forms except for the listed differences. Worn and carried gear keeps its original form.

lines: Speed · 30 ft., fly 50 ft. in raven or hybrid form

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A Barovian shapeshifter that can appear human, raven, or as a winged hybrid with a raven head and black feathers.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Skills Insight +4, Perception +6. Damage immunities: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks unless made with silvered weapons. Passive Perception 16. Languages: Common. It cannot speak in raven form.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Shapechanger. The wereraven can spend an action to become a raven, a raven-humanoid hybrid, or its human form. Its other statistics carry across forms except for size and the listed flight. Its gear does not change with it. It returns to human form when it dies.
Mimicry. It can imitate simple sounds it has heard. A listener can identify an imitation with a DC 10 Wisdom (Insight) check.

gm.title: Actions

Multiattack (human or hybrid only). Make two weapon attacks, with at most one Hand Crossbow attack.
Beak (raven or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1 piercing in raven form or 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing in hybrid form. A humanoid hit must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or contract wereraven lycanthropy.
Shortsword (human or hybrid only). Melee weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing.
Hand Crossbow (human or hybrid only). Ranged weapon attack +4, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing.

gm.title: Player lycanthropy
lines:
A character keeps its own statistics except for the changes listed here. It gains the printed nonhumanoid speeds, damage immunities, traits, and actions that require no equipment, plus proficiency with the lycanthrope's natural attacks. Use the listed natural weapon damage. The character cannot speak in animal form.
Only a humanoid that is not already a lycanthrope saves against the curse when hit by a curse-bearing attack. The Constitution save DC is 8 + the attacking lycanthrope's proficiency bonus + its Constitution modifier. A character who resists the curse keeps their usual alignment and personality in humanoid form. The full moon forces them into animal or hybrid form until it wanes. A character who embraces the curse acquires the lycanthrope's alignment and can eventually learn to shift at will. The DM can take control of the character until the curse is removed. Remove Curse can end an acquired curse. A natural-born lycanthrope needs Wish.
Raise Strength to 17 if lower. Use Strength for natural weapon attack and damage rolls. The Pounce save DC is 8 + the character’s proficiency bonus + its Strength modifier.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: A dancing light that reaches Cerilia just ahead of an opening Shadow World portal. It draws vitality from the living before the portal pulls it back.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Tiny to Small floating creature. Chaotic neutral.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Rare in Cerilia and the Shadow World. Solitary, appearing 1d3. Active at night in Cerilia or any time in the Shadow World. Feeds on Cerilian life energy. High intelligence 13–14. Treasure Q. Size 1–4 ft. across. Morale 15–16. No bloodline, blood abilities, or Perception. Seeming lesser.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Life drain. One touch for 2d8 damage to a Cerilian creature. It feeds on that loss without adding the damage to its own HP. A non-Cerilian takes a 1d8 burn instead and provides no nourishment.

gm.title: Feeding near the portal
lines: When Cerilian characters are within a quarter mile, there is a 50% chance the creature feeds on their life energy rather than the surroundings. Affected Cerilians save vs. poison or take 2d6 damage. When Cerilians are on the Shadow World side of a portal about to open and a will o’Shadow is present, make that save with a 1-point penalty. It is normally invisible on that side of the portal.

gm.title: Defenses and tactics
lines: Mundane weapon blows deal normal damage. Detect invisibility and shadow magic are the only magic specifically noted as effective. Magical light makes the creature invisible until the light goes out. Its lesser Seeming can camouflage it with blur, color spray, dancing lights, or hypnotic pattern. It usually avoids direct combat, attacks to replace lost energy when provoked, and tries to flee at 5 HP or fewer.

gm.title: Portal clues
lines: One to three lights can precede a portal by 1 minute to 3 hours. A larger light means it is closer to opening. Nearby vegetation may stay wilted for 1d4 days per round the portal was open. The lights communicate with one another through their movement.

gm.title: False tomb encounter
lines: The entrance seals 1 round after the coffin is opened if the illusory sunlight strikes its plaque. Dispel Magic on the light prevents the trigger. Once the entrance seals, the wine rises 1 ft. a round and everyone rolls initiative. On round 3, three wine weirds emerge from the northwest, northeast, and southeast cisterns and attack everyone in the room. On round 12, the room fills. Apply underwater combat with 5 ft. of visibility. Water breathing gives no protection against drowning in wine. The block rises and the wine drains after 10 minutes.

gm.title: Description
lines: Winter eladrin embody sorrow. Their tears freeze on their faces, and the cold around them reflects their grief.

lines:
Magic Resistance. The eladrin has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Sorrowful Presence. A non-eladrin creature starting its turn within 60 ft. makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns and whenever this eladrin damages it, ending the effect on a success. When the creature succeeds or the effect ends, it gains immunity to any eladrin's Sorrowful Presence for 24 hours.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 16). No material components are required.

gm.title: Encounter
lines: Six winter wolves attack from the mist. They retreat into cover between attacks and focus on prone characters. The icy ground is difficult terrain and imposes disadvantage on saves to avoid falling prone. The wolves circle a fortified camp, harry sentries and prevent sleep. Characters who cannot sleep gain one level of exhaustion. If any reach two levels of exhaustion, the wolves attack. The pack gives up if the party gets 8 miles from the campsite. To run for it, count the party as having traveled 8 hours. At the end of each additional hour, each character makes a Constitution save at DC 10 plus hours traveled past 8 or gains one exhaustion level. Eluding the wolves awards 250 XP per character.

gm.title: MCDM demon soul rules
lines:
Soul count. Use the printed starting total or roll the listed dice. Souls spent on a feature are deducted from the total. A demon can accumulate souls without a maximum.
Soul Devourer. When the demon drops a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure, the demon consumes its soul, adds 1 to its soul count, and the creature dies. Only Wish can restore it to life.
Lethe. At 0 souls, the demon has advantage on attacks and disadvantage on saving throws, and its Intelligence is 3. On each turn it must use its movement to get as close as possible to the nearest creature it senses with Soulsight. If able, it must then use its action to attack that creature and attempt to kill it. It can pursue no other goal until its soul count rises.
Soulsight. Within the creature’s listed radius, it perceives creatures other than Constructs and Undead. This counts as seeing them for its features. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.

lines: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing while in dim light or darkness.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Wretched Pack Tactics. The sorrowsworn has advantage on an attack against a creature while an ally that is not incapacitated is within 5 ft. of that creature. Otherwise, its attack rolls have disadvantage.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage and the sorrowsworn attaches to the target. While attached it cannot attack, moves with the target without spending movement, and deals 6 (1d10 + 1) necrotic damage to the target at the start of each of its own turns. The sorrowsworn can spend 5 ft. of movement on its turn to detach. Any creature, including the target, can use its action to detach it.

gm.title: Description
lines: A limbless, wingless burrower that liquefies loose soil with vibrations. The Gruul sometimes lure it toward settled districts.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Earth Tremors. When a creature first comes within 30 ft. of the moving wurm on a turn, it makes a DC 20 Dexterity save. Failure deals 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage and knocks it prone. A ground-anchored object or structure that first comes within the same distance on a turn takes 10 (3d6) force damage.
Siege Monster. The wurm deals double damage to objects and structures.
Tunneler. The wurm burrows through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and leaves a 10-ft.-diameter tunnel.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 24 (5d6 + 7) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit must pass a DC 20 Dexterity save or be swallowed. It is blinded and restrained inside, has total cover from external attacks and effects, and takes 17 (5d6) acid damage at the start of each of the wurm’s turns. If a creature inside deals 30 or more damage to the wurm in one turn, the wurm makes a DC 21 Constitution save at that turn’s end. On a failure it regurgitates all swallowed creatures, which land prone within 10 ft. When the wurm dies, swallowed creatures are no longer restrained by it. They can spend 20 ft. of movement to exit prone.

gm.title: Description
lines: This massive worm gathers secrets and hires bodyguards to enforce its bargains. In a fight it can roll over opponents and crush their equipment.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Very rare in hot climates. Omnivore. Exceptional intelligence (15–16). Treasure A, D. Fanatic morale (17–18). Length 30–45 feet. One wurmling per encounter, with at least 1d4 trusted guards and sometimes up to 4d10. Its wider organization usually has 100–200 retainers.

gm.title: Hit Dice, THAC0 and XP
lines:
10 HD: THAC0 11.
11–12 HD: THAC0 9.
13–14 HD: THAC0 7.
15 HD: THAC0 5.
Start at 5,000 XP for 10 HD, then add 1,000 XP per additional HD.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite and tail. Bite for 2d8 and lash with the tail for 1d8. Treat its Strength as 20 when grabbing or holding something.
Roll over. With enough room, it can roll onto up to three human-sized or smaller targets. Save vs. paralysis to avoid it. On failure, take 1d4 damage per wurmling Hit Die. It can remain on top for the same damage each subsequent round. On a failed initial save, each of the victim’s possessions must save vs. crushing blow or be destroyed.

gm.title: Defenses
lines: Magic resistance 2% per HD. Immune to scarlet pimpernel hallucinations and mood-altering abilities or proficiencies such as fast talk, intimidation, and bardic charm. Add +3 to saves against mind-altering spells and mind-affecting Legacies.

gm.title: Skills and Red Curse
lines: As a thief of level equal to its HD, it can open locks, find and remove traps, move silently, hear noise, and read languages. It knows one spoken language per 2 HD. It has legend lore and local history, plus information-related nonweapon proficiencies as a thief of the same level. Gain Legacies as an Inheritor of level equal to HD. A 10 HD specimen has five Legacies, a 12 HD specimen has six, and a 15 HD specimen has seven. The first needs no crimson essence. Later Legacies need crimson essence to activate at acquisition and stay permanently. It needs cinnabryl to maintain them. Typical choices are Anti-Poison, Crimson Fire, Digging, Farsight, Red Shield, Shape Stone, and Temperature, or choices suited to Eusdria.

gm.title: Description
lines: A wyvern hunts from the air and strikes with its jaws and venomous tail.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Sting attack.
Bite. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Sting. Melee attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 24 (7d6) poison damage. The target is Poisoned until the start of the wyvern's next turn.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A rocky-scaled dragon with two hind legs, wings used as forelimbs on the ground, and a long, acid-delivering stinger.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Athletics +6, Perception +5. Acid damage immunity. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 15. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Stubborn Rage. The wyvern is immune to Frightened and Stunned while below half its maximum HP or within 60 ft. of another wyvern it can see or hear.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Stinger attack and one Bite attack. The wyvern can replace either one of those attacks with Tail Sweep.
Stinger. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit 13 (3d6 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 14 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 7 (2d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute. The target repeats this save at the end of each of its turns. A success ends the ongoing acid damage. Cure Ailment or Lesser Restoration also ends the effect.
Bite. Melee weapon attack +6, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 16 (2d12 + 3) piercing damage. A Large or smaller target is also Grappled (escape DC 13) and Restrained during the grapple. The wyvern cannot Bite another target until that grapple ends.
Tail Sweep. Each creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a DC 14 Strength save. A failure deals 14 (2d10 + 3) bludgeoning damage and pushes the creature up to 10 ft. away from the wyvern.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Seek. The wyvern takes the Search action.

gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: 7 + 7 × the caregiver’s level in hit points, with one d8 Hit Die per caregiver level.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A two-legged dragon with leathery wings, rocky indigo scales and a hooked tail stinger.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Armor class 13 + PB. Strength save +3 + PB. Perception +2 + PB. Acid damage immunity. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 12 + PB.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Learning to Fly. The wyvern has a flying speed of 10 × PB feet.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Stinger). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Acidic Sting (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack at 15-ft. reach. A hit deals extra acid damage equal to PB.
Level 3, Liquefied Meal (5 Ferocity). A Large or smaller creature within 5 ft. makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB. On a failure it falls Prone and takes 1d4 + PB acid damage. The wyvern gains temporary hit points equal to the acid damage dealt.
Level 5, Tail Sweep (8 Ferocity). Every creature in a 15-ft. cone makes a Strength save against DC 10 + PB. On a failure it takes PBd6 bludgeoning damage and is pushed up to 10 ft. away.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Enraged Protector. When a visible creature within 30 ft. of the wyvern drops its caregiver to 0 HP or scores a critical hit against the caregiver, the wyvern can move up to its speed. If it ends within 5 ft. of that attacker, it can make a signature attack against it.

gm.title: Mystic connection
lines: Acid-Enhanced. At 9th level, a Beastheart with this companion and Mystic Connection can spend a bonus action once per long rest to exude acid from their hands for 1 minute. Their melee weapon attacks and unarmed strikes deal an extra 1d8 acid damage during this time.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Actions

Claws, humanoid form. Two claw attacks deal 1d6 damage apiece.

gm.title: Bearer benefits
lines: The Margrave of Slagovich can use poison three times per day as the reverse of the priest spell neutralize poison. This power works regardless of telepathic contact or whether the bearer carries the coat of arms.

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Voice of the Ages is a storm dragon who has forgotten his own name and much of the lore he once knew.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saving throws Con +15, Wis +10, Cha +12. Arcana +21, History +21, Nature +21, Perception +10, Religion +21. Immune to lightning and thunder damage and to Charmed, Dazed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, and Stunned. Blindsight 120 ft., truesight 60 ft., passive Perception 20. Speaks all languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Static Shield (3/day). Turn a failed save into a success. His sight, blindsight, and truesight are limited to 30 ft. until the start of his next turn.
Storm of the Gods. His lightning and thunder damage ignore resistance.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, 15-ft. reach, one target. Hit 20 (2d10 + 9) piercing plus 5 (1d10) lightning damage. He can move the target up to 20 ft. in any direction.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, 10-ft. reach, one target. Hit 16 (2d6 + 9) slashing plus 7 (2d6) thunder damage and knocks the target Prone.
Fulminating Breath (recharge 5–6). Creatures in a 120-ft.-long, 30-ft.-wide line make DC 23 Dexterity saves. On a failure, they take 66 (12d10) lightning damage and have disadvantage on saves until the end of Xaantikorijek's next turn. A success halves the damage and avoids the disadvantage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Lightning Discharge. Make one Bite attack. On a hit, deal an extra 11 (2d10) lightning damage to that target and to one other enemy within 60 ft. of it.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Voice of Negation. When a visible creature within 60 ft. uses an action or bonus action to cast a spell, it makes a DC 23 save using its spellcasting ability. Failure deals 16 (3d10) thunder damage and prevents casting until the end of the creature's turn. It keeps its spell slot and action.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Each action is available once per encounter, after an enemy finishes a turn. Use them in any order, at most one per round.
1. Voice of Reverence. Choose creatures within 60 ft. Each falls Prone on a failed DC 20 Wisdom save and takes 22 (4d10) thunder damage if it stands before the end of Xaantikorijek's next turn.
2. Fulguration. Until the end of his next turn, he turns into lightning. During this time he resists all damage, fits through 1-inch gaps without squeezing, can move through creatures' spaces, and provokes no opportunity attacks. The first time he enters a creature's space each turn, that creature takes 16 (3d10) lightning damage.
3. Voice of the Ages. Enemies within 60 ft. who hear him make DC 20 Wisdom saves. Failure deals 44 (8d10) psychic damage, knocks the target Prone, and prevents it from standing for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each turn. A success halves the damage and avoids the other effects.

gm.title: Description
lines: A half-elf sorcerer with fine draconic scales, Xandala wants the Ring of Winter for its power and longevity. She claims to be Artus Cimber’s daughter to get help finding him.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Quickened Spell (3/day). When she casts a spell with a casting time of one action, she can cast it as a bonus action instead.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Quarterstaff. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage, or 4 (1d8) if wielded in two hands.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
9th-level sorcerer. Charisma, spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks.
At will: Acid Splash, Fire Bolt, Light, Mage Hand, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots): Chromatic Orb, Feather Fall, Shield.
2nd level (4 slots): Invisibility, Misty Step.
3rd level (3 slots): Fireball, Fly.
4th level (3 slots): Ice Storm, Polymorph.
5th level (1 slot): Dominate Person.

gm.title: Encounter context
lines: She plans to use Dominate Person to make Artus surrender the Ring of Winter, then escape with Fly. Her companion Summerwise is a Pseudodragon who thinks the quest is reckless. Good-aligned characters can win Summerwise over. Xandala trusts her draconic ancestry to carry her to greatness and treats others as fools.
